text.text: The following are reasons for the failure of agricultural policies in West Africa except

key_point.text: Agro stations helped — not a failure reason.

body.text: Service stations supported farmers; vague policy, negations and obsolete tools failed them.

trap.text: Obsolete-tools tempts as help, but it failed — stations helped.

text.text: An entrepreneur is encouraged to adopt division of labour in production because it
leads to increased cost of production and lower output
brings about equal cost and employment opportunities
leads to increased output and lower cost of production

key_point.text: Division pays in output per cost.

body.text: Specialised labour raises output and cuts unit cost. Higher costs, more jobs and equal outcomes miss it.

trap.text: More-jobs tempts as benefit, but the encouragement is output-per-cost.

text.text: In determining the growth of a country's population, infant mortality is a component of

key_point.text: Infant deaths count in death rate.

body.text: Mortality enters deaths, not fertility or migration. Net, fertility and immigration rates exclude it.

trap.text: Fertility tempts as birth-talk, but infant deaths are deaths.

text.text: One disadvantage of inflation is that?

body.text: Salaries fixed while prices climb lose real worth. Rising living, gaining earners and losing businessmen invert it.

trap.text: Businessmen-lose tempts as victim-talk, but debtors among them gain.

text.text: The market supply curve slopes upwards from left to right indicating that
two commodities can be supplied at the same time
at a lower price, more is supplied
at a lower price, less is supplied

key_point.text: Upward supply: dearer price, more supplied.

body.text: Lower price means less supplied — the law of supply. Joint supply, taxes and reverse readings miss it.

trap.text: Lower-more tempts as demand-talk, but supply slopes up.

text.text: The exploitation of mineral resources constitutes which form of production?

body.text: Extraction stage. Secondary makes, tertiary serves, services serve.

trap.text: Secondary tempts as industry, but extraction is primary.

text.text: Which of the following factors does not encourage the location of industries?

body.text: Firms avoid unpredictable states. Markets, infrastructure and state siting attract.

trap.text: State-siting tempts as location-talk, but instability is the repellent.

text.text: Which of the following is not a feature of economic under development?

body.text: Monoculture, short lives and inequality fit; productivity does not.

trap.text: Inequality tempts as developed-trait, but it fits underdevelopment too.

text.text: The function that distinguishes commercial banks from the central bank is that the former
is a leader of last resort

key_point.text: Only commercial banks take public deposits.

body.text: Accepting deposits defines them against the central bank. Debt service, forex and last-resort are central jobs.

trap.text: Last-resort tempts as banking, but it is central-only.

text.text: The following are advantages of large scale agriculture except
integration of crop and animal farming?

body.text: Mechanisation defines large farming; simple implements mark small. Sophisticated tools, integration and jobs fit large.

trap.text: Jobs tempts as benefit, but implements mark the scale.

text.text: When the death rate for old people and the infant mortality rate are high, with no migration, there will be in the population a higher number of

key_point.text: High deaths at both ends leave the young standing.

body.text: Old and infants die most; the middle-young dominate counts. Children, women and old options misread the pyramid.

trap.text: Old-people tempts as survivors, but they die most.

text.text: If an increase in the price of crude oil led to an increase in the prices of kerosene and grease,then kerosene and grease are in

key_point.text: One price shock moving two goods is joint supply.

body.text: Kerosene and grease flow together from crude. Competitive, composite and market readings split them.

trap.text: Competitive tempts as related-goods, but joint moves together.

text.text: Which of the following best describe token money?
Coins and notes made of poor quality materials
Money in the vault of commercial banks
Money with face value higher than its material content

body.text: Face above content defines token money. Circulating cash, poor materials and vault money miss it.

trap.text: Poor-materials tempts as token-talk, but the gap is value-over-content.

text.text: In calculating the Gross National Product (GNP) by the income approach, all the following are included except
direct taxes paid by persons and companies

key_point.text: Direct taxes never enter income sums.

body.text: Wages, rents and pensions count; direct taxes are transfers, not factor pay.

trap.text: Wages tempts as taxable, but taxes themselves are excluded.

text.text: One advantage of a sole proprietorship is that
it makes an increase in the volume of business possible
it can be managed without conflicts
the sole proprietor raises money from the public
there is no limit to the number of people who may bring in capital

body.text: Sole control avoids disputes. Scale, public money and many capitals belong to bigger forms.

trap.text: Scale tempts as advantage, but harmony is the one's edge.

text.text: The United Nation Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD) is a forum designed specifically for discussing the
religious affairs in the Southern Africa
educational needs of the developed countries
better terms of trade in the world
political conflicts in the United Nation Security Council

key_point.text: UNCTAD talks trade terms for the South.

body.text: Better deals for developing trade is its forum. Religion, education and Security-Council politics belong elsewhere.

trap.text: Security-Council tempts as UN-talk, but UNCTAD is trade.

text.text: Which of the following serves as a banker's bank?

key_point.text: Banks bank at the central bank.

body.text: Banker's bank by definition. Commercial, development and mortgage banks are customers there.

trap.text: Commercial tempts as banking, but bankers'-bank is central.

text.text: A country's balance of payments is in deficit when
a country's payments for imports of invisible goods are greater than her receipts from exports of invisible goods
the total receipts from her export of visible and invisible goods are greater than her payments for visible and invisible imports
the total payments for visible and invisible imports are greater than the total receipts from her exports of visible and invisible goods
It can record a surplus on current account of her balance of payments accounts

body.text: Payments exceed receipts on visibles plus invisibles. Surplus readings invert it.

trap.text: Receipts-greater tempts as balance-talk, but deficit is payments-ahead.

text.text: Population growth rate can be calculated as
birth rate- death rate + immigrants - emigrants

key_point.text: Growth nets births, deaths and migration.

body.text: Births minus deaths plus immigrants minus emigrants. Dropped terms unbalance it.

trap.text: Births-minus-deaths tempts as enough, but migration completes it.

text.text: In the event of bankruptcy, owners of joint-stock companies lose

key_point.text: Failure costs shareholders their stake only.

body.text: Limited liability caps loss at capital. Private property, dividends-only and double-asset readings miss the shield.

trap.text: Private-property tempts as loss, but limited means stake-only.

text.text: Development plans in West Africa tend to deviate from their targets mainly due to

body.text: Instability breaks implementation. Education, population and manpower trail.

trap.text: Manpower tempts as capacity-talk, but politics kills plans first.

text.text: An agricultural production process which uses more machinery relative to labour is referred to as

key_point.text: Machines over men is capital intensive.

body.text: High capital-labour ratio defines it. Land, scale and commerce readings miss the ratio.

trap.text: Large-scale tempts as machine-ish, but intensity is the ratio.

text.text: Which of the following institutions is concerned with expanding developing countries' commodity trade?
United Nations Conference on Trade and Development (UNCTAD)

key_point.text: UNCTAD speaks commodity trade for developing states.

body.text: Same forum as 76938: trade expansion. WTO, ECA and AfDB do other work.

trap.text: WTO tempts as trade-talk, but commodity-trade expansion is UNCTAD's.

text.text: The transfer of ownership of a public enterprise to individual and firms is called

body.text: Ownership transfer defines it. Restructuring, commercialisation and nationalisation move otherwise.

trap.text: Commercialisation tempts as market-talk, but ownership moves only in privatization.

text.text: Which of the following equation is appropriate for determining the Net Domestic Product (NDP)
NDP = GDP x Net Income from abroad
NDP - GDP + Net Income from abroad

body.text: GDP minus capital consumption. GNP variants and multiplied forms miss it.

trap.text: GNP-minus tempts as depreciation-talk, but NDP starts from GDP.

text.text: The charging of different prices to different groups of buyers for the same goods or services is called?

body.text: Charging groups differently defines it. Competition forms and determination miss the split.

trap.text: Monopoly tempts as pricer, but the practice named is discrimination.

text.text: Which of the following is necessary for the survival of small firms in West Africa?
Government assistance in the form of loans and tax holidays

key_point.text: Small West African firms live on state help.

body.text: Loans and tax holidays keep them alive. High costs, weak collateral and land access kill instead.

trap.text: Land-access tempts as help, but the lifeline named is state aid.

text.text: The greatest foreign exchange earner for Nigeria before the advent of petroleum was

key_point.text: Before oil, Nigeria farmed for forex.

body.text: Agriculture led exports pre-petroleum. Handicraft, mining and manufacturing trailed.

trap.text: Mining tempts as export, but farming led.

text.text: Which of the following is not a function of an insurance company?
Collection of deposits from the public for investment
Encouragement of savings habits through life assurances
Mobilization of funds through premiums collected
Granting of loans on long-term basis for investment

body.text: Insurers pool risk; banks take deposits. Savings, premiums and long loans fit insurers.

trap.text: Long-loans tempts as financial, but deposits belong to banks.

text.text: One disadvantage of direct taxes is that they

body.text: Assessed payers dodge. Rigidity, progressivity and allocation miss the leak.

trap.text: Progressive tempts as feature, but evasion is the disadvantage.

text.text: The reward to land as a factor of production is

body.text: Factor payments pair: land-rent, labour-wage, capital-interest, enterprise-profit.

trap.text: Wage tempts as payment, but land's is rent.

text.text: Acceptability , durability, homogeneity , and portability are all attributes of good

key_point.text: Good money is acceptable, durable, uniform and portable.

body.text: The classic attribute list. Markets, governments and banks are not money.

trap.text: Markets tempts as money-place, but attributes belong to money.

text.text: The Consumers Co-operative society is owned by?

body.text: Members contribute, own and share. Debenture holders, committees and government serve other forms.

trap.text: Government tempts as big-owner, but co-ops are member-owned.

text.text: The primary objective of the Nigerian Industrial Development Bank (NIDB) is the provision of provision of loans to?

body.text: Industrial Development Bank lends long to industry. Estates, transport and farms borrow elsewhere.

trap.text: Farmers tempt as borrowers, but NIDB is industrial.

text.text: an annual statement showing transaction within a country
the relationship between a country's receipt from visible and invisible trade
an account that shows a country's payment to other countries
the relationship between a country's visible exports and imports

body.text: Exports minus imports of goods. Invisibles, payments and domestic statements belong elsewhere.

trap.text: Visible-plus-invisible tempts as trade, but BOT is goods alone.

text.text: Which of the following will shift the demand curve for cocoa to the right?
A rise in the price of cocoa
A fall in the quantity demanded of cocoa

key_point.text: Richer buyers shift cocoa demand right.

body.text: Income rises lift demand at every price. Price rises move along; taxes and quantity falls shift otherwise.

trap.text: Price-rise tempts as demand-talk, but shifts come from non-price factors.

text.text: A stock exchange is a market that
deals with the exchange of commodities
deals with purchase and sales of securities
exchanges treasury bills for bills of exchange

body.text: Shares and bonds change hands there. Commodities, fish and bills trade elsewhere.

trap.text: Treasury-bills tempts as paper, but the market named trades securities.

text.text: Which of the following forms of economic integration is a member nation free to impose duty against non-members

key_point.text: Free-trade members keep own outside tariffs.

body.text: No common external duty, unlike customs unions. Common markets and communities bind deeper.

trap.text: Customs-union tempts as free-trade-ish, but it imposes common duty.

text.text: A rise in government expenditure can lead to
lower importation of raw materials by industries

body.text: Demand stimulus inflates. Unemployment, profits and imports move otherwise.

trap.text: Unemployment tempts as spending-worry, but the first effect is inflation.

text.text: A budget is balanced when expected total revenue is

body.text: Expected totals match. Less, greater and expected-greater unbalance.

trap.text: Greater-revenue tempts as healthy, but balance is equality.

text.text: Another term for equilibrium price is

body.text: Market-clearing price is its other name. Demand, satisfactory and floor prices differ.

trap.text: Price-floor tempts as price-talk, but clearing is equilibrium.

text.text: Table I above illustrates the law of

key_point.text: Falling marginal utility fills the table.

body.text: The figure's MU column drops 10, 5, 2, 1, 0 as units rise — textbook diminishing marginal utility.

trap.text: Variable-proportion tempts as production-talk, but the table is utility.

text.text: Harmonised monetary and fiscal policies is a feature of

body.text: Monetary-plus-fiscal union is deepest integration. Customs, common market and free trade stop shallower.

trap.text: Common-market tempts as deep, but harmony peaks at economic union.

text.text: If 20% rise in the price of Whisky leads to a 30% increase in quantity demanded of Schnapps, the cross elasticity of demand is

body.text: Percentage change in schnapps over whisky price change. Other quotients misdivide.

trap.text: 3.0 doubles instead of dividing 30 by 20.

text.text: The major achievement of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS) is that it has
made possible the use of common currency.
increased members allegiance to former colonial masters.
widened the market for goods produced.

body.text: Bigger goods market is its headline gain. Common currency, colonial ties and capital mobility trail.

trap.text: Common-currency tempts as integration, but market-widening is the achievement.

text.text: A typical example of landforms produced by marine erosion is a

body.text: Typical landform stated. Spits, beaches and mud-flats deposit, not erode.

trap.text: Spit tempts as coastal-word, but erosion builds stacks.

text.text: The main advantage of the chain survey over the prismatic compass survey is that the former
does not require a base map
closes its boundaries with no correction

body.text: Main advantage stated for small surveys. Base maps, self-closing and portability miss it.

trap.text: Portability tempts as field-talk, but the edge is accuracy.

text.text: On a population map of the world, all but one of the following appear generally as regions of low population density

body.text: All-but-one low-density: Amazon, deserts and Antarctica empty; Java crowds.

trap.text: Amazon tempts as tropical-empty, but the exception is Java.

text.text: Which of the following type of agriculture would you expect to find around a big city in an industrial society, such as in Europe?

body.text: Expected near big European cities: perishable milk. Grain, ranching and fish sit farther.

trap.text: Grain tempts as farming, but city-fringe is dairy.

text.text: Smooth oval hills composed mainly of boulders or glacial sands and gravels are known as

body.text: Smooth glacial hills stated. Arêtes, moraines and eskers differ.

trap.text: Moraine tempts as glacial-word, but ovals are drumlins.

text.text: Name the most important industrial mineral of Ghana
Which of the following zones is the least industrialized in Nigeria?

body.text: Zone stated. Port Harcourt, Lagos and Kaduna all out-industrialise it.

trap.text: Kaduna-Zaria tempts as northern, but least is Lokoja-Ajaokuta.

text.text: Which of the following most accurately describes the climate of coastal lands which are adjacent to cool ocean currents?

body.text: Described as winter rain, summer drought. Monsoon, year-round and summer-rain miss it.

trap.text: Summer-rain tempts as tropical, but cool-current coasts dry Mediterranean.

text.text: Two factors that promote rapid chemical weathering in the tropics are

key_point.text: Tropics rot rock hot and wet.

body.text: Two factors stated. Cold-wet, hot-arid and hot-dry miss the pair.

trap.text: Hot-arid tempts as tropical, but chemical needs humidity.

text.text: Which of the following factors must account for the rapid increase in world population during the twentieth century?

body.text: Must-account factor: rapidly decreased death rates. Food, abolition and births miss the driver.

trap.text: Births tempts as population-talk, but the driver is fewer deaths.

text.text: Which of the following towns is NOT a pre-colonial town?

body.text: NOT pre-colonial stated. Bida, Ilorin and Ibadan predate colonisers.

trap.text: Ibadan tempts as big-old, but colonial-born is Enugu.

text.text: growing crops and rearing animals on a given land area
growing grains and root crops on the same piece of land
keeping poultry and rearing pigs on one and the same farm
mixed cultivation of wheat, barley, and oats

body.text: Implies stated on one land area. Grains-only, poultry-pigs and cereals-only narrow it.

trap.text: Grains-only tempts as mixed-word, but mixed is crops-plus-animals.

text.text: In which of the following countries is commercial grain farming an important occupation?

body.text: Commercial grain stated. Spain, Kenya and Nigeria trail it.

trap.text: Nigeria tempts as home, but grain belts mean Canada.

text.text: The main use of the Abney Level in surveying is to determine the

body.text: Main use: angle of inclination. Areas, heights and locations belong to other tools.

trap.text: Spot-height tempts as survey-talk, but Abney reads inclination.

text.text: Which of the following phenomena is not directly related to the rotation of the Earth?
unequal solar radiation on the earth's surface

body.text: NOT rotation-related: seasonal change rides revolution. Day-night, sunshine hours and radiation tilt on spin.

trap.text: Sunshine-hours tempts as daily, but seasons are revolution.

text.text: Temperature is to isotherms as air pressure is to

body.text: Temperature-isotherm analogy stated. Isopleths, isolines and contours generalise or heighten.

trap.text: Contours tempts as line-talk, but pressure is isobars.

text.text: Which of the following factors least explains the fast-growing population in Africa?

key_point.text: Schooling girls curbs births, so it explains growth least.

body.text: Female education drives fertility down — it opposes rapid growth rather than explaining it. Disease control, transport access and death-rate decline all feed growth. Recorded c; corrected to a.

trap.text: Transport tempts as development-talk, but schooling actively curbs growth.

body.text: Means stated: household consumption. Cash, extensive and intensive differ.

trap.text: Cash tempts as farming-aim, but subsistence feeds home.

text.text: Scandinavia is noted for its hardwood timber
The North Sea is a great fishing area
Katanga is a copper mining region
The Ruhr is a great industrial region

body.text: Incorrect statement: boreal softwoods rule. North Sea fish, Katanga copper and Ruhr industry all hold.

trap.text: Ruhr tempts as checkable, but the false one is hardwood.

text.text: Which statement is NOT true of the Middle Belt in Nigeria
there are insect pests and disease carriers

body.text: NOT-true asked: productive soil debates aside, pests and sparseness hold — none of the above is the NOT.

trap.text: Unproductive-soil tempts as middle-belt, but the answer is none-above.

text.text: Which of the following has the highest mean annual rainfall?

body.text: Highest mean stated. Lagos, Accra and Lome trail it.

trap.text: Lagos tempts as wettest-known, but Freetown tops.

text.text: Which is not exported by the Republic of South Africa?

body.text: Not exported stated. Wines, maize and wool all ship.

trap.text: Maize tempts as African-crop, but the exception is coffee.

text.text: Which pair of activities would you NOT find in an equatorial climate? 1. Commercial grain farming. 2. rice cultivation. 3. lumbering. 4. plantation agriculture. 5. dry farming

body.text: NOT-found pair: commercial grain (1) and dry farming (5). Rice, lumbering and plantations all belong.

trap.text: Lumbering tempts as temperate, but it thrives equatorial.

text.text: Which of the following currents has a warming influence upon the coast along which it flows?

body.text: Warming influence stated. Benguela, Labrador and Canaries all cool.

trap.text: Canaries tempts as current-talk, but warming is Mozambique.

text.text: Inter-regional trade between countries in West Africa is promoted mainly by
competition among the nations in Africa
deliberate government policies in recent times

body.text: Promoted mainly by deliberate government policies. Rivalry, sameness and colonial ties miss it.

trap.text: Colonial-ties tempts as history, but promotion is policy.

text.text: What is the Nile Valley best known for?

body.text: Best known for among options: Aswan power. Industry, navigation and commerce trail it.

trap.text: Navigation tempts as river-talk, but fame is power.

text.text: How were the major mountain belts of the world produced?

body.text: Produced by folding. Wind, ice and weathering wear, not raise.

trap.text: Weathering tempts as mountain-talk, but belts fold.

text.text: Which ONE of the following statements about the railway lines of Africa is false?
The railway lines of Africa generally run from the coast inland
There is no trans-continental railway in Africa which can be compared with the Trans-Siberian Railway in length or importance
Africa's railway lines are all of uniform gauge
Few railway lines in Africa cross from one country to another

key_point.text: African rails share no single gauge.

body.text: False statement: gauges vary. Coast-inland, no-transcontinental and few-crossings all hold.

trap.text: Coast-inland tempts as pattern (true), but false is uniform gauge.

text.text: The Middle Belt of West Africa is NOT characterised by one of the following. Which one?

key_point.text: Middle Belt exports little cash crop.

body.text: NOT characteristic: few towns, low density and fragmentation hold; export cropping does not.

trap.text: Fragmentation tempts as standout, but the NOT is export crops.

text.text: The length of a year is 365(\(\frac{1}{4}\))days because that is the time it takes.
the sun to revolve around its orbit
the moon to revolve once around the earth
the earth to revolve once round the sun
the earth to rotate on its axis

body.text: 365 and a quarter: earth round sun. Sun-orbiting, moon-orbiting and spinning miss it.

trap.text: Spinning tempts as daily (24h), but years orbit.

text.text: Which of the following gradients is the steepest?

body.text: Gradient 1-in-N steepens as N shrinks; 134 beats 153, 351 and 531. The recorded key misread the ratio. Recorded c; corrected to a.

trap.text: 1-in-153 tempts as small-number, but 134 is smaller.

text.text: When the gradient of a river channel changes from a steep to a gentle angle, the main activity of the river will be

body.text: Steep-to-gentle shift: rivers drop load. Eroding, terracing and deepening belong to steeps.

trap.text: Eroding tempts as river-work, but gentle deposits.

text.text: Which one of the following countries has an export trade which is dominated by a single mineral?

body.text: Single-mineral export: copper Zambia. Central African Empire, Kenya and Uganda diversify.

trap.text: Kenya tempts as exporter, but single-mineral is Zambia.

text.text: Which of the following lakes owes its origin mainly to faulting?

body.text: Origin mainly faulting: Rift Valley lake. Superior, Victoria and Chad differ.

trap.text: Victoria tempts as African-lake, but fault-born is Malawi.

text.text: If a map at a scale of 1:50,000 is reduced by half, what is the new scale of the map?

key_point.text: Halving the map doubles the denominator: 1:100,000.

body.text: Reduction shrinks the image, so each unit covers twice the ground. 1:25,000 enlarges instead. Recorded b; corrected to a.

trap.text: 1:25,000 tempts as halved-number, but reduction doubles ground-per-unit.

text.text: The wearing away of the sides and bottom of a river's channel is called
The greatest volume of shipping across the Atlantic Ocean is
between North America and South America

body.text: Greatest volume stated. Africa-involved routes trail it.

trap.text: Africa-America tempts as Atlantic, but volume is Europe–N.America.

text.text: Which of the following provides the best location for a bakery?
Near a large market for bread
Near a regular source of flour
In an area of cheap labour
Near a source of good clean water

body.text: Best location: perishable bread sells near buyers. Flour, labour and water trail freshness.

trap.text: Flour tempts as input-talk, but bakeries hug markets.

text.text: Which purpose is NOT served by the Kainji Dam?
provision of water of domestic use all over Nigeria
generation of electricity for use all over Nigeria

key_point.text: Kainji lights homes; it waters none nationwide.

body.text: NOT served: domestic water all over Nigeria. Power generation, research institutes and lake fishing all serve — the recorded key named generation, Kainji's very purpose. Recorded d; corrected to b.

trap.text: Generation tempts as dam-talk (it serves), but unserved is nationwide tap water.

text.text: mining, furniture making, and cocoa processing

body.text: Broadly classified stated. Fishing-mining-food and mining-furniture-cocoa mix levels.

trap.text: Fishing-mining-food tempts as industries, but broad is three sectors.

text.text: Great Britain and Germany are trading partners of West African countries from

key_point.text: Britain and Germany stand in West Europe.

body.text: Trading partners from stated region. South America, Far East and North America miss the map.

trap.text: Far-East tempts as trade-talk, but both stand West-European.

text.text: The most significant factor which accounts for the rapid growth in the population of the capital cities of West Africa is

body.text: Most significant factor: rural-urban migration. Rallies, sports and tourism miss the millions.

trap.text: Rallies tempts as crowd-talk, but growth is migration.

text.text: What is the temperature around an aeroplane flying at an altitude of 4000 metres if the temperature on the earth surface is 40 °C?

body.text: Lapse 6.5 per 1000 over four kilometres. 66 warms, 26 and 12 misrate.

trap.text: 26 tempts as near-miss, but the drop is 26 from 40.

text.text: Which of the following wave actions is a process of erosion

body.text: Erosion process: hydraulic pounding. Saltation, traction and suspension transport.

trap.text: Suspension tempts as wave-word, but erosion is hydraulic.

text.text: Which of the following factors is a major boost to tourism?
Higher dependency ratio of the population

body.text: Major boost stated. Dependency, transport-modes twice-listed miss the pull (c/d duplicate noted).

trap.text: Transport tempts as tourism-need, but the boost is publicity.

text.text: The heavy, dark soil associated with floodable valley bottoms is a

body.text: Waterlogged stated. Lateritic, ferrallitic and podzolic differ.

trap.text: Lateritic tempts as tropical-soil, but valley-wet is hydromorphic.

text.text: Urban floods are mainly caused by

body.text: Mainly caused by blocked drains and waterways. Farm clearance, dams and shelter belts miss town.

trap.text: Dams tempts as water-talk, but urban floods choke drains.

text.text: A feature produced by water in desert areas is

body.text: Feature stated. Barchans, yardangs and zeugens blow, not flow.

trap.text: Yardang tempts as desert-word, but water cuts wadis.

text.text: Which of the following are characteristics of most large cities? They I. have large populations II. are administrative centers III. are religious centers IV. are commercial centers

key_point.text: Big cities pack people and trade.

body.text: Characteristics: I large populations, IV commercial centres. Administration and religion vary.

trap.text: Administration tempts as city-mark, but the pair is people-plus-trade.

text.text: A block mountain is formed as a result of

body.text: Formed by faulting. Erosion, fissures and vulcanicity differ.

trap.text: Vulcanicity tempts as mountain-talk, but blocks fault.

text.text: Which of the following is an important line of longitude?

body.text: Important line stated. Arctic, Antarctic and Cancer latitude.

trap.text: Cancer tempts as famous-line, but longitude is Meridian.

text.text: The temperature reading at the peak of a volcano is 6°C. What will be the temperature at the foot of the volcano, which is 3000 metres from the surrounding low land?

body.text: Lapse reversed over three kilometres. 13.5, 23.5 and 5.5 misrate.

trap.text: 23.5 tempts as near-miss, but the climb is 19.5.

text.text: Which of the following is not a process of chemical weathering?

body.text: NOT chemical: frost action is physical. Hydrolysis, oxidation and carbonation all react.

trap.text: Oxidation tempts as weathering (it is), but the NOT is frost.

text.text: Which of the following distinguishes rotation from revolution?
Revolution causes day and night, while rotation causes season
The earth rotates on its axis while it revolves round the sun on an elliptical orbit
A complete revolution takes 24 hours, while rotation marks a year
Rotation causes variation in the lengths of day and night, while revolution causes rising and falling of tides

body.text: Distinguishes stated: axis-spin versus elliptical orbit. Swapped and tide readings invert it.

trap.text: Swapped-readings tempt as pairing, but spin is axis.
