text.text: The process by which plants absorb water from the soil through their roots is

body.text: Soil water crosses root hairs down a water-potential gradient through membranes. Diffusion is general, photosynthesis makes food, transpiration loses water.

trap.text: Transpiration pulls the column but absorption at the root is osmosis.

text.text: The bright colouration of the flower of a flowering plant is an adaptation for

body.text: Colour attracts pollinators to the flower's reproductive business. Growth, excretion and respiration do not need advertising.

trap.text: Growth tempts as plant business, but petals exist for pollination.

text.text: Use the diagram above to answer the questions that follow The endocrine gland that is located in the part labelled I is

key_point.text: Part I in the head is the pituitary.

body.text: The figure places I at the brain base — the pituitary seat. Thyroid and parathyroid sit at the neck, adrenals at kidneys.

trap.text: Thyroid tempts as famous gland, but the head location fixes pituitary.

text.text: One of the components of peripheral nervous system is

body.text: PNS is nerves to and from the cord: sensory in, motor out. Brain, cord and cerebellum are central.

trap.text: Spinal cord tempts as connected, but it is central, not peripheral.

text.text: When the cotyledons appear above the soil during germination is called

body.text: Epi-above, hypo-below: carried-up seed leaves define epigeal. Hypogeal keeps them down; epicotyl and hypocotyl name stem parts.

trap.text: Hypocotyl names the stem below, not the pattern.

text.text: The type of teeth used for tearing in man is labelled

key_point.text: Tearing teeth are canines: II on the figure.

body.text: The pointed single-cusp teeth flank incisors — canines tear. Molars (IV) grind, incisors cut.

trap.text: IV tempts as biggest teeth, but size grinds; points tear.

text.text: Which of these animals create their natural habitats in burrows?

key_point.text: Burrows are dug homes: bush rat.

body.text: Rats excavate burrows; doves nest, chameleons perch, snails carry shells.

trap.text: Snails tempt as ground-dwellers, but shells are carried, not dug.

text.text: The green-brown colour of grasshopper's body in dry grass field is an adaptation for

body.text: Crypsis hides from predators and prey. Predation, mating and mimicry are other interactions.

trap.text: Mimicry copies another species — matching grass is background, not a model.

text.text: Which of the following is an advantage of cross fertilization?
Individuals produced are less adapted to local environment
It leads to the production of healthier offspring.
It leads to the production of weak offsprings.

body.text: New gene combinations mask recessives — hybrid vigour. Inbreeding depression and weak offspring are selfing's costs.

trap.text: Inbreeding depression is the reverse outcome, not the advantage.

text.text: In most vertebrates, the common basic plan with a skull, vertebral column and a pair of girdle is an evidence of evolution from

key_point.text: Shared body plans argue comparative anatomy.

body.text: Skull, column and girdles across vertebrates show common descent in structure. Molecules, fossils and embryos argue other lines.

trap.text: Fossils tempt as evolution evidence, but body plans are anatomy.

text.text: Example of animal exhibiting mating colouration is

key_point.text: Breeding colours flash in the agama lizard.

body.text: Red-headed males signal — classic mating colouration. Grasshoppers hide, chameleons shift, leopards spot for camouflage.

trap.text: Chameleon tempts on colour change, but agama shows the mating display.

text.text: Which of the following is the excretory organ in birds?

body.text: Metanephric kidneys pass uric acid to the cloaca. Nephridia, Malpighian tubules and green glands belong to worms, insects and crustaceans.

trap.text: Malpighian tempts as excretory, but that is insects.

text.text: Whose theory of evolution supports that characters acquired through use or disuse are transmitted to offspring?

key_point.text: Use and disuse inheritance is Lamarck.

body.text: Lamarck (spelled Larmark in the options) taught acquired transmission. Darwin selected, Mendel counted, Morgan mapped.

trap.text: Darwin tempts as evolution, but natural selection is not use-inheritance.

text.text: When calyx of a flower is joined together, it is called

body.text: Gamo- joined, poly- free; sepal whorl versus petal whorl. Gamopetalous joins petals instead.

trap.text: Gamopetalous tempts on joined, but the whorl here is calyx.

text.text: Which of the following statements about poliomyelitis is correct?
It affects both young and old.
There is no vaccination against the disease.
It is capable for paralysing the limbs.

body.text: Enterovirus attacks motor neurones; it is viral, vaccine-prevented, and strikes mainly the young.

trap.text: Bacterial misnames the agent — polio is a virus.

text.text: What is the phenotype of the offspring produced in F\(_1\)?
The cortex of a herbaceous stem is made up of

key_point.text: Herbaceous cortex is soft tissue: parenchyma plus collenchyma.

body.text: No wood means no sclerenchyma bulk and no xylem in cortex. Sclerenchyma stiffens woody parts instead.

trap.text: Any option with sclerenchyma overbuilds a soft stem.

text.text: The most advanced spermatophyte that forms the largest group of plant kingdom is the

body.text: Largest plant group by far. Ferns, cones and gymnosperms are smaller and older.

trap.text: Gymnosperm tempts as seed plant, but angiosperms outnumber them hugely.

text.text: Which of the following is a medium of transportation in animal cells?

body.text: Blood carries gases, food and waste between tissues. Latex, cytoplasm and cell sap stay local.

trap.text: Cytoplasm tempts as cell medium, but transport between cells is blood.

text.text: The part labelled I is the

body.text: The zoomed figure puts I's line on the large dark body's edge; II marks a mitochondrion. Cytoplasm and vacuole lie elsewhere.

trap.text: Mitochondrion tempts because II points at one — but I is the nucleus.

text.text: Which of these is an estuarine habitat?

key_point.text: Brackish meeting water is a lagoon.

body.text: Lagoons mix sea and fresh — estuarine. Rivers, lakes and ocean are single-salinity.

trap.text: Ocean tempts as salty, but estuarine means the mixture.

text.text: The mouth parts of a grasshopper are adapted for

body.text: Mandibles cut and grind vegetation. Piercing-sucking belongs to bugs and mosquitoes.

trap.text: Sucking tempts on mouthparts generally, but grasshoppers chew.

text.text: The following are factors that affect the population growth of an organism except

key_point.text: Natality grows populations; the rest check them.

body.text: Predators, food shortage and disease limit growth — natality (births) raises it. The question asks the exception.

trap.text: Disease tempts as killer only, but all three others limit while natality adds.

text.text: The innermost layer of mammalian epidermis is

key_point.text: Deepest epidermis is the malpighian layer.

body.text: Cell division happens at the base; cornified, granular and capillary layers sit above or outside.

trap.text: Cornified is the dead surface — the opposite end.

text.text: In a cross involving a heterozygous red flower plant (Rr) and a white flowered plant (rr), what is the probability that the offspring will be Rr?

key_point.text: Rr by rr gives half Rr.

body.text: Punnett: Rr, Rr, rr, rr — 1/2 heterozygous red. Not all, not a quarter, never 2.

trap.text: 1 tempts as dominant always wins, but half the offspring are rr white.

text.text: The structure that helps in the formation of cilia and flagella is

key_point.text: Basal bodies build cilia and flagella.

body.text: Centrioles template the microtubule axoneme. Plastids photosynthesise, Golgi packages, lysosomes digest.

trap.text: Golgi tempts as organelle-maker, but cilia grow from centrioles.

text.text: The vertebrate bone responsible for the attachment of the abdominal muscles is

key_point.text: Abdominal muscles hang off lumbar vertebrae.

body.text: The lumbar spine anchors the abdominal wall. Sacral, thoracic and cervical serve pelvis, ribs and neck.

trap.text: Thoracic tempts as trunk, but the abdomen is lumbar territory.

text.text: The canine teeth are prominent in which group of animals?

body.text: Tearing flesh needs canines; herbivores grind, parasites suck, omnivores mix.

trap.text: Omnivores tempt as canine-carriers, but prominent canines mark carnivores.

text.text: Translocation of manufactured food in plants is through the

body.text: Translocation of photosynthate is phloem flow. Xylem lifts water, pericycle and endodermis are root layers.

trap.text: Xylem tempts as transport, but it carries water up, not food down.

text.text: The most advanced organism in an evolutionary trend among the following is

key_point.text: Segmented worm outranks flat, round and hollow: earthworm.

body.text: Annelids add segmentation and coelom over platyhelminths, nematodes and cnidarians. Hydra sits lowest here.

trap.text: Hydra tempts as animal, but it lacks even bilateral symmetry.

text.text: One of the following adapts baobab tree to savanna habitat.

key_point.text: Baobab survives drought behind thick bark.

body.text: Fire- and water-loss protection in savanna. Tap roots, broad leaves and deciduous stems miss its signature.

trap.text: Broad leaves would lose water — baobab sheds small ones instead.

text.text: Albinism is a disorder caused by

body.text: Two copies for the phenotype; melanin production fails. Sebum and melanin excess describe other conditions.

trap.text: Over-production of melanin is the reverse — albinos under-produce.

text.text: An example of a reflex action is

body.text: Spinal arc without cortical control. Writing, talking and walking are voluntary.

trap.text: Walking tempts as automatic, but it stays voluntary.

text.text: Which of the following is an example of vestigial structure?

key_point.text: The appendix does nothing now: vestigial.

body.text: Shrunken caecum remnant. Trunks, wings and gills all work.

trap.text: Bird wings tempt as useless-for-humans, but vestigial means useless-to-owner.

text.text: The correct base pair in DNA molecule is

key_point.text: A pairs T, C pairs G — Chargaff.

body.text: Adenine-thymine is the correct pair. All cross-pairings break the rule.

trap.text: Cytosine-adenine mixes purine with pyrimidine wrongly.

text.text: Population replacement among species of organisms in a given habitat under competition is due to

key_point.text: Replacement under competition is natural selection.

body.text: Fitter variants hold the habitat. Climax, dominance and bare survival name other outcomes.

trap.text: Survival of the fittest tempts as phrase, but the mechanism asked is selection.

text.text: Appendix in humans and caecum in herbivores are evidences of evolution from

key_point.text: Appendix and caecum are leftover structures: vestigial organs.

body.text: Reduced organs arguing descent. Fossils, anatomy-at-large and embryos argue otherwise.

trap.text: Comparative anatomy is the wider field — vestigial organ is the precise evidence.

text.text: A form of adaptive colouration that helps animals to remain unnoticed is

key_point.text: Blending by light and shade is countershading.

body.text: Dark back, pale belly dissolve outline. Hibernation, aestivation and migration hide in time, not in sight.

trap.text: Migration tempts as hiding, but countershading hides in plain view.

text.text: Genetically Modified Organisms (GMO) food products are of benefit to farmers because they are

body.text: Pest- and herbicide-resistant varieties. Susceptible, low-quality and low-yield are the reverse.

trap.text: Low quality inverts the benefit — resistance is the product.

text.text: The variation that can be applied in crime detection is

body.text: Unique, unchanging ridge patterns. Tongue rolling, height and colour vary continuously or irrelevantly.

trap.text: Height tempts as measurable, but it is continuous and non-unique.

text.text: The date palm is commonly planted in Sahel zone of

key_point.text: Date palm country in the Sahel is Borno.

body.text: Chad-basin oases around Borno grow dates. Kastina, Plateau and Taraba lie outside the belt.

trap.text: Plateau tempts as northern, but dates follow the Sahel proper.

text.text: The region of a flower stalk attached to flower parts is

key_point.text: Flower parts sit on the receptacle.

body.text: The stalk tip bears all whorls. Corolla, calyx and pedicel are parts or stalk, not the seat.

trap.text: Pedicel is the stalk itself — parts attach at its tip, the receptacle.

text.text: Which of the following processes takes place in the carbon cycle?

body.text: Combustion returns carbon to CO2 in the cycle. Nitrification, evaporation and transpiration move nitrogen or water.

trap.text: Transpiration tempts as cycling, but it cycles water.

text.text: An instrument used in measuring plants growth is

key_point.text: Growth is measured with an auxanometer.

body.text: Stem elongation on a calibrated arc. Hygrometers, barometers and thermometers read humidity, pressure, temperature.

trap.text: Thermometer tempts as lab glass, but growth needs length, not heat.

body.text: Single-celled green alga: Protophyta. Tracheophytes, pteridophytes and bryophytes are land plants.

trap.text: Bryophyta tempts as simple-green, but Chlamydomonas is unicellular.

text.text: The part of the flower that is brightly coloured and attract pollinating agents such as insects is labelled

key_point.text: Petals advertise: III on the figure.

body.text: The figure's III marks the showy petal whorl; I is stigma, II anther, IV sepal. Bright colour means pollinator attraction.

trap.text: Stigma receives pollen — it does not advertise.

text.text: Which of the following blood groups will clump when mixed with anti-a antibody serum?

key_point.text: Anti-A clumps A and AB blood.

body.text: A antigens meet anti-A: A and AB carry them. B and O lack them.

trap.text: B only inverts the antigen — anti-A ignores B.

text.text: Which of these is the correct arrangement of tissues in herbaceous roots from the circumference to the center?
piliferous layer, cortex, pericycle, vascular tissue and pith
piliferous layer, cortex ,vascular tissues, pericycle and pith
piliferous layer, pericycle ,vascular tissues, cortex and pith
piliferous layer, cortex , vascular tissues, pith and pericycle

key_point.text: Root layers run piliferous, cortex, pericycle, vascular, pith.

body.text: Outside in: hairs, cortex, pericycle ring, stele, centre. Every other order misplaces the pericycle.

trap.text: Pericycle-before-cortex options forget the ring sits inside the cortex.

text.text: The part labelled I is the

key_point.text: I caps the snail: the shell.

body.text: The figure puts I on the coiled shell. Foot, head and collar sit below.

trap.text: Foot tempts as biggest mass, but I marks the top shell.

text.text: The function of the organelle labelled II is to
coordinate the activities of the cell

key_point.text: The snail's coordinator is its nerve centre: II.

body.text: Ganglia at II integrate stimuli. Energy, transport in and out belong to other systems.

trap.text: Transport-within tempts on circulation, but coordination is nervous.

text.text: The cell component that stores waste products is the

body.text: Plant vacuoles store excreta and toxins. Golgi packages, walls support, lysosomes digest.

trap.text: Lysosome tempts as waste-related, but storage is vacuolar.

text.text: Which of these plants is considered to be common in an estuarine habitat?

body.text: Salt-tolerant pneumatophore forests fringe brackish water. Plantain, gmelina and iroko are inland.

trap.text: Gmelina tempts as plantation tree, but estuaries grow mangrove.

text.text: Renal artery branches and divides into a mass of blood capillaries in the Bowman's capsule called

body.text: Capillary ball where filtration starts. Tubule, pelvis and nephron name downstream or whole parts.

trap.text: Nephron tempts as kidney unit, but the tuft itself is glomerulus.

text.text: Glucose → ethanol + CO\(_2\) The chemical reaction above represents the process of

key_point.text: Sugar to alcohol plus gas is fermentation.

body.text: Yeast turns glucose to ethanol and CO2. Oxidation burns, glycolysis splits, photosynthesis builds.

trap.text: Glycolysis tempts as sugar-splitting, but ethanol plus CO2 is fermentation.

text.text: Agglutination occurs in blood transfusion when the
antigen and antibody in the donor and the recipient are incompatible
donor and recepient belong to different races
same antibodies from donor and recipient fuse together
donor and the recipient belong to the same blood group

body.text: Incompatible donor-recipient pairs clump. Same group, same antibodies or race do nothing.

trap.text: Same-group tempts as mixing, but matching never clumps.

text.text: Part of the littoral zone of the marine habitat above the high tide mark, wetted by spray of water from breaking of waves is referred to as the

key_point.text: Spray-wet rock above high tide is splash zone.

body.text: Supralittoral fringe wetted by spray. Benthic is bottom, subtidal always submerged, intertidal between tides.

trap.text: Intertidal tempts as shore, but above-high-tide spray is splash zone.

text.text: Which of the following differentiates photosynthesis from respiration?
It occurs both during the day and night.
It occurs in both plants and animals.

body.text: Photolysis splits water and releases O2; respiration consumes it. Day-night and plant-animal options blur the line.

trap.text: Occurs-day-and-night describes respiration, not photosynthesis.

text.text: Use the diagram above to answer the questions that follow The part labelled II is the
In which state of Nigeria is Obudu game reserve located?

key_point.text: Obudu sits in Cross River State.

body.text: The ranch highlands are Cross River's. Anambra, Akwa Ibom and Rivers hold other reserves.

trap.text: Rivers tempts on delta geography, but Obudu is Cross River.

text.text: In Nigeria, the major climatic factor that determines the distribution of organisms is

body.text: Vegetation belts track precipitation. Temperature, humidity and light follow.

trap.text: Temperature tempts globally, but Nigerian zones answer to rain.

text.text: The slender and stick-like shapes of the stick insect is a structural adaptation for

key_point.text: Stick shape hides: protection and defence.

body.text: Resembling twigs fools predators. Water, mating and escape miss the camouflage.

trap.text: Escaping tempts as survival, but stillness-plus-shape is defence.

text.text: In a community with limited resources, the less vigorous species are eliminated due to

body.text: The less vigorous lose contested resources. Disease, drought and births act otherwise.

trap.text: Drought tempts as killer, but elimination-by-rivalry is competition.

text.text: Which of the following statements is correct about sedimentation of a given soil?
Largest and medium size particles settle at the bottom.
Remains of decaying organic matter settles at the bottom.
Largest soil particles remain suspended in water.

body.text: Decaying organics stay afloat in the sedimentation jar; sand, silt and clay settle by size.

trap.text: Bottom-settling options invert the observation — organics ride the top.

text.text: Which of the following exists at the organ level of organization?

key_point.text: A bulb is an organ: onion.

body.text: Storage shoot with tissues — organ level. Euglena, hydra and paramecium sit at cell or tissue grade.

trap.text: Hydra tempts as multicellular, but it never reaches organs.

text.text: The organization that provides emergency needs of children globally is

body.text: UN children's fund handles crisis needs. NMA, WHO and UNIDO serve doctors, health policy and industry.

trap.text: WHO tempts as UN-health, but children's emergencies are UNICEF's mandate.

text.text: A repeating unit of a very large DNA molecule is made up of

body.text: Sugar, phosphate and base in one unit, repeated. Each part alone is not the unit.

trap.text: Nitrogenous base tempts as information, but the repeating unit adds sugar and phosphate.

text.text: Which of the following is an effect of carbon monoxide on humans?
Major cause of respiratory tract infections.
Reducing oxygen carrying capacity of blood

body.text: CO locks haemoglobin as carboxyhaemoglobin. Infections, clots and mutations belong elsewhere.

trap.text: Respiratory infection tempts as breathing harm, but CO starves oxygen delivery.

text.text: The constantly dividing cells found at the apex of roots and stem during growth is

body.text: Root and shoot tips grow from apical tissue. Intercalary, lateral and bare meristematic name other sites or the tissue generally.

trap.text: Meristematic alone is too broad — apex specifies apical.

key_point.text: Calcium is a macronutrient; the rest are micro.

body.text: Plants need Ca in bulk; B, Fe and Zn in traces.

trap.text: Iron tempts as familiar nutrient, but it is required in micro amounts.

text.text: The longest single bone in human is the

key_point.text: The thigh bone is longest: femur.

body.text: Femur outruns humerus, scapula and sternum in every skeleton.

trap.text: Humerus tempts as long bone, but the femur is the longest.

text.text: One characteristic which differentiates bats from birds is that bats

body.text: Bats are mammals; birds lack them. Four-chambered hearts, night habits and warm blood are shared.

trap.text: Nocturnal tempts as batty, but some birds fly nights too — milk is decisive.

text.text: The part labelled II is the

key_point.text: II in the female tract is the uterus.

body.text: The figure centres II on the womb between tubes and cervix. Cervix, vagina and ovary sit around it.

trap.text: Ovary tempts as reproductive, but II marks the middle chamber.

text.text: The biological association between bacteria and protozoa in the rumen of cattle is an example of

key_point.text: Rumen microbes and host both gain: symbiosis.

body.text: Bacteria digest cellulose, cattle absorb products — mutual. Commensalism, parasitism and predation split benefits unevenly.

trap.text: Commensalism tempts as harmless, but the host gains too — mutual.

text.text: In which of the following organisms does niche differentiation serve as a means of reducing intraspecific competition?

key_point.text: Tilapia partition niches to ease crowding.

body.text: Age- and size-class feeding zones cut intraspecific contest. Deer, pigeon and toad lack the textbook case.

trap.text: Pigeon tempts as flocking, but the cited case is tilapia.

text.text: Seaweeds and Barnacles are common flora and fauna found in which of these habitats?

body.text: Rocky-shore sea life is marine. Terrestrial, estuarine and fresh lack one half of the pair.

trap.text: Estuarine tempts as salty, but the classic pairing is marine.

text.text: Competition between cow and goat for scarce grasses during dry season can be described as

body.text: Different species contesting grass. Intraspecific is same-species; predation and commensalism are other relations.

trap.text: Intraspecific tempts as competition, but species differ here.

text.text: The oxygen transported to all parts of the body during blood circulation is used for the

key_point.text: Circulated oxygen burns food for energy.

body.text: Aerobic respiration releases energy from glucose using carried O2. Waste removal, growth and carboxyhaemoglobin miss the use.

trap.text: Growth tempts as oxygen-needing, but the direct use is energy release.

text.text: The presence of tiny, non-functional hind leg bones inside a whale's body suggests that whales
are not related to land animals.
evolved from ancestors that had legs
have never had legs in their evolutionary history
bones serve a major function in swimming

key_point.text: Whale hip bones whisper land ancestors.

body.text: Vestigial legs argue descent from walking mammals. Unrelated, legless-ever and swimming-function misread them.

trap.text: Swimming-function tempts as useful, but they are functionless remnants.

text.text: The genetic make up of an organism is referred to as the

body.text: Genes possessed, not shown (phenotype), nor counted (nucleotide, karyotype).

trap.text: Phenotype tempts as genetics-talk, but makeup means genotype.

text.text: The ability of chameleon to change its colour to that of the environment is for

body.text: Background matching fools predators. Invitation, attraction and attack use colour oppositely.

trap.text: Attack tempts as active use, but hiding is defence.

text.text: One of the following is a reflex action

body.text: Irritant arc fires without decision. Walking, dancing and crying stay voluntary.

trap.text: Crying tempts as automatic, but it remains controllable.

text.text: Proteins are macromolecules made of smaller units called

body.text: Peptide bonds link amino units. Glycerol, carboxylic and fatty acids build lipids.

trap.text: Fatty acid tempts as bio-molecule, but proteins are amino chains.

text.text: Transparency of water is measured using a

key_point.text: Clarity is read on a secchi disc.

body.text: Lowered white disc vanishing depth measures transparency. Hygrometers, barometers and anemometers read humidity, pressure, wind.

trap.text: Barometer tempts as instrument, but clarity is optical.

text.text: The maximum number of organisms that the resources in the habitat can support is referred to as

key_point.text: The habitat ceiling is carrying capacity.

body.text: Maximum sustainable headcount on given resources. Maximum population names a count, working and operating potentials are economics.

trap.text: Maximum population tempts as same words, but capacity is the resource concept.

body.text: Xero-dry: water conservers. Mesophytes need moderate water, hydrophytes live wet, sporophytes are a spore stage.

trap.text: Sporophyte tempts as plant-word, but it names a life stage, not a habitat type.

text.text: An example of a plant whose flower is dispersed by wind is

body.text: Cypsela fruits carry pappus parachutes. Schizocarps split, caryopses are grains, capsules burst.

trap.text: Capsule tempts as seed-holder, but wind dispersal here means the plumed cypsela.

text.text: An example of a saprophytic organism is

key_point.text: Bread mould eats dead matter: rhizopus, saprophyte.

body.text: Rhizopus digests dead organic matter externally. Bladderwort and sundew trap live prey; mistletoe parasitises living hosts.

trap.text: Mistletoe tempts as plant-feeding-plant, but it feeds on living hosts — parasitic, not saprophytic.

text.text: Absorption of nutrients in ferns is through

body.text: Pteridophytes bear real roots for absorption; rhizome is the underground stem, rhizoid belongs to mosses, hyphae to fungi. The recorded key named the stem — corrected here with the reason on record.

trap.text: Rhizome tempts as underground, but stems do not absorb — roots do. Recorded key was D (rhizome); corrected to roots.

text.text: Which of these insects has a piercing and sucking mouthpart?

body.text: Stylets puncture skin and draw blood. Cockroaches bite-chew, butterflies and moths sip.

trap.text: Butterfly tempts as sucker, but only mosquito pierces first.

text.text: The segregation of genes occurs during

body.text: Meiosis segregates homologues into gametes. Mitosis copies, fertilization joins, transmission describes the whole.

trap.text: Fertilization joins what segregation split — opposite directions.

text.text: Which of the following is a behavioural adaptation of animals for avoiding adverse weather conditions?

body.text: Dormancy through adverse seasons. Hiding, stillness and swelling are momentary, not seasonal.

trap.text: Hiding tempts as avoidance, but seasonal dormancy is hibernation.

text.text: A medium of transportation of materials in plants is the

key_point.text: Plant sap carries materials: cell sap.

body.text: Dissolved substances ride cell sap through the plant. Xylem and phloem are the pipes, cytoplasm the local medium.

trap.text: Xylem tempts as transport tissue, but the medium asked is the sap.

text.text: The artery that carries blood to the heart is

key_point.text: Heart muscle feeds via coronary arteries.

body.text: Coronaries branch to the heart wall itself. Pulmonary serves lungs, renal kidneys, aorta the body.

trap.text: Aorta tempts as heart-adjacent, but it carries blood away, not to the muscle.

text.text: The relationship between fungus and alga in lichen is an example of

key_point.text: Fungus plus alga helping each other is mutualism.

body.text: Lichen partners trade protection for food — both gain. Parasitism, commensalism and predation split gains unevenly.

trap.text: Commensalism tempts as harmless, but the alga gains too — mutual.

text.text: The digestive enzyme pepsin is active in

body.text: Stomach pH activates pepsin; alkali, neutral or both-media options denature or stall it.

trap.text: Neutral tempts as safe middle, but pepsin needs acid.

text.text: One of the following is an epidemic diseases in Nigeria

body.text: Water-borne Vibrio outbreaks define the epidemic2598 pattern. Malaria is endemic, schistosomiasis focal, polio near-eradicated.

trap.text: Malaria tempts as killer, but endemic is not epidemic.

text.text: The two - hoofed toes of camels allow easy walking on desert because of

key_point.text: Wide feet spread load on sand: enlarged surface.

body.text: Camel toes splay broad to float on desert. Narrow, long or elongated feet would sink.

trap.text: Long tempts as desert-y, but width spreads weight, not length.

text.text: Which of these animals uses buccal respiration?

key_point.text: Toads pump air through the mouth: buccal respiration.

body.text: Amphibian buccal floor ventilates. Tilapia gills, birds lungs-air-sacs, grasshoppers tracheae.

trap.text: Grasshopper tempts as small-breather, but buccal is amphibian.

text.text: The prevalence of pests and diseases which affect plants and animals in a terrestrial habitat is

key_point.text: Pests and disease are living pressures: biotic.

body.text: Organisms acting on organisms. Abiotic, edaphic and climatic are non-living.

trap.text: Climatic tempts as habitat-wide, but pests are biotic.

text.text: Use the illustration above to answer the question that follows What is the genotypic ratio of the F\(_2\) generation?

body.text: The figure shows RR, Rr, Rr, rr — one of each homozygote, two heterozygotes. 3:1 is the phenotype ratio.

trap.text: 3:1 tempts as the famous ratio, but genotypes count 1:2:1.

text.text: A structure associated with an open circulatory system is

body.text: Insects and molluscs flood body cavities, not closed vessels. Veins, arteries and arterioles are closed-system pipes.

trap.text: Artery tempts as blood-carrier, but open systems lack them.

text.text: Long beak with saw-like edges is an adaptation in

key_point.text: Serrated fish-grippers belong to the pelican.

body.text: Long bill with saw edges holds slippery fish. Woodpeckers chisel, kingfishers spear, ducks strain.

trap.text: Duck tempts as water-bird, but saw edges are the pelican's grip.

text.text: The zone in an ecosystem that provides habitat for living organism is referred to as

body.text: The living shell across rock, water and air. Atmosphere, lithosphere and environment name parts or surroundings.

trap.text: Environment tempts as everything, but the inhabited zone is biosphere.

text.text: An example of application of variation is

body.text: Variation fingerprinting proves parentage. Sex, population and fitness use variation otherwise.

trap.text: Sex determination tempts as genetics-use, but fathers means paternity.

text.text: The level of organization in onion bulb is

key_point.text: Bulb is an organ, asked again.

body.text: Same organ-level answer as 74511's set: storage shoot. System, tissue and cell undercount.

trap.text: Tissue tempts as multicellular, but bulb integrates tissues — organ.

text.text: The type of germination in which the cotyledons remain below the soil surface is

key_point.text: Seed leaves staying down is hypogeal.

body.text: Hypo-below versus epi-above. Plumule and micropyle name other parts.

trap.text: Epigeal is the reverse pattern — cotyledons carried up.

text.text: The stamen of a flower consists of

key_point.text: Stamen is stalk plus head: filament and anther.

body.text: Support plus pollen sac. Ovary, stigma, sepals and petals belong to other whorls.

trap.text: Ovary tempts as flower-centre, but stamen is male: filament and anther.

text.text: Chemical breakdown of large food molecules into smaller and soluble substances is the function of

key_point.text: Chemical digestion happens in the duodenum.

body.text: Pancreatic and intestinal juices dissolve food there. Ileum absorbs, large intestine and rectum handle water and waste.

trap.text: Ileum tempts as small-intestine, but breakdown peaks in the duodenum.

text.text: The type of holozoic nutrition where organisms feed on both plant and animal substances is

body.text: Plants plus animals. Saprophytes eat dead matter, herbivores and carnivores one kingdom each.

trap.text: Saprophytic tempts as mixed-feeding, but it means dead matter, not both kingdoms.

text.text: The molecule with the highest number of lone pair of electrons is

key_point.text: CO2 carries four lone pairs, the most here.

body.text: H2O has 2, NH3 has 1, CH4 has 0; CO2 has two oxygens with 2 each = 4.

trap.text: CH4 tempts as biggest molecule, but lone pairs are unshared electrons, not atoms.

text.text: The composition of petroleum varies because it is a

key_point.text: Petroleum varies because it is a mixture.

body.text: Crude is many hydrocarbons mixed; composition shifts by source. A pure hydrocarbon would be fixed.

trap.text: Hydrocarbon tempts on content, but content is not composition — mixtures vary, compounds do not.

text.text: In the table above, the two compounds that will combine in the presence of an acid-catalyzed compound, V is

key_point.text: Ester V comes from alcohol I plus acid IV.

body.text: From the figure: I is ROH, IV is RCOOH; acid-catalysed esterification gives V = RCOOR'.

trap.text: III and IV pairs two acids — esterification needs the alcohol half.

text.text: An example of an alkaline gas is

key_point.text: Ammonia is the classic alkaline gas.

body.text: NH3 dissolves to give OH- and turns damp red litmus blue. HCl and NO2 are acidic; N2 is neutral.

trap.text: NO2 tempts as nitrogen-containing, but its solution is acidic, not alkaline.

text.text: The dusty and sand particles present in the air is an example of

key_point.text: Visible dust in air is a suspension.

body.text: Sand particles are large, undissolved, and settle — textbook suspension. Emulsions are liquid-in-liquid; saturated solutions are dissolved.

trap.text: Dispersion is the general term, not the answer the options want.

text.text: Calculate the pH of 0.001M KOH solution.

key_point.text: 0.001 M KOH gives pOH 3, so pH 11.

body.text: KOH is strong: [OH-] = 1e-3, pOH = 3, pH = 14 - 3 = 11.

trap.text: 3 answers pOH instead of pH — the scale has two ends.

text.text: The acid used in making baking soda and soft drink is

key_point.text: Tartaric acid is the recorded food acid here.

body.text: Baking powder pairs it with bicarbonate; soft-drink acidity is food-acid territory. Fatty and boric acids have no food role.

trap.text: Citric tempts for soft drinks, but the recorded key is tartaric — one acid per both uses as set.

text.text: The compound CH\(_3\)CH(NH\(_2\))CH\(_2\)CH\(_2\)CH\(_3\) is an example of a

key_point.text: One carbon on nitrogen is a primary amine.

body.text: CH3CH(NH2)- is R-NH2: primary. Secondary needs two carbons on N, tertiary three.

trap.text: Secondary tempts on the long chain, but class counts N-substituents, not chain length.

text.text: Nitrogen, a component of air is used for

key_point.text: Nitrogen's headline industrial use is nitric acid.

body.text: NH3 via Haber then Ostwald to HNO3. Cooling agents, margarine and oil are not nitrogen chemistry.

trap.text: Margarine borrows hydrogenation, a hydrogen story, not nitrogen.

text.text: 2Na + Cl\(_2\) → 2NaCl In the reaction above, the specie that undergoes reduction is

body.text: Na 0 to +1 oxidises; Cl2 0 to -1 reduces. The species reduced is elemental chlorine.

trap.text: Cl- is already reduced — reduction happens to Cl2 going in, not Cl- coming out.

text.text: The sublimation of solid to gas involves

body.text: Solid to gas breaks lattice bonds with no liquid step — heat in. Melting and vaporisation are its halves.

trap.text: Osmotic diffusion belongs to solutions, not phase changes.

text.text: The products of the thermal decomposition of ammonium trioxonitrate(v) are

key_point.text: Ammonium nitrate gives nitrous oxide and steam.

body.text: NH4NO3 -> N2O + 2H2O on heating. NO2 needs hotter routes; O2 alone is not the product.

trap.text: NO2 tempts as nitrogen-oxide-plural, but the thermal route stops at N2O.

text.text: 2X + 2HCl → 2XCl + H\(_2\) In the equation above, X is

key_point.text: A +1 metal with HCl giving H2 points at potassium here.

body.text: 2X + 2HCl -> 2XCl + H2 means X is monovalent and vigorous: K of the options. Mg, Ca, Ba are divalent with different stoichiometry.

trap.text: Mg tempts as reactive, but divalent metals give XCl2, not XCl.

text.text: Alkanoic acids have higher boiling points than alkanols because
alkanoic acids are more volatile than alkanols
alkanols are more polar than alkanoic acids
alkanoic acids form stronger hydrogen bonds

key_point.text: Acids dimerise through stronger hydrogen bonds.

body.text: Two -COOH groups pair up, holding molecules tighter than alkanol chains. Volatility and size miss the bonding.

trap.text: Larger molecules tempts, but acids and comparable alkanols are similar sizes — bonding decides.

text.text: Water drops are spherical in shape because of

body.text: A sphere minimises surface for a volume; tension does the minimising. Polarity enables it, density and viscosity do not shape it.

trap.text: Polarity tempts as the cause, but tension is the shaping force.

text.text: In the electrolysis of brine using neutral electrode, which ion is discharged at the anode?

key_point.text: Chloride discharges at the anode in brine.

body.text: At the anode anions oxidise; concentrated Cl- beats OH-. Na+ and H+ go to the cathode.

trap.text: OH- discharges only in dilute brine — concentration picks chloride here.

text.text: The time required to deposit 4.5g of copper from CuSO\(_4\) solution by passing a current of 2.5 Amperes is (Cu = 64g ; 1F = 96500C/mol)

key_point.text: Faraday: time is mass times zF over current times mass number.

trap.text: Halving the electron count answers 2714 — copper(II) needs two faradays per mole.

text.text: Which of the following pairs of elements will exhibit diagonal relationship?

key_point.text: Boron and silicon share the diagonal.

body.text: B/Si is the classic group 13/14 diagonal pair. Be pairs with Al, Li with Mg.

trap.text: Li/Al mixes two real diagonals — Li goes with Mg, Be with Al.

text.text: The following is not a water pollutant?

key_point.text: Oxygen gas is not a pollutant.

body.text: Warm effluent, fertilisers and degradable waste all degrade water; dissolved O2 is what clean water holds.

trap.text: Biodegradable waste tempts as harmless, but its decay load pollutes.

key_point.text: Acid radicals are the negative ions: carbonate, sulphate, nitrate.

body.text: Only option c lists three anions. The others smuggle in Mg2+, Na+, K+ cations.

trap.text: Cations sit beside real radicals in every distractor — radicals are the anions.

text.text: What accounts for the low melting and boiling points of covalent molecules?

key_point.text: Weak intermolecular forces mean low melting and boiling.

body.text: Covalent molecules separate easily because little holds them. Shared pairs and shapes describe the molecule, not the lattice.

trap.text: Shared electron pairs tempts as bonding, but boiling breaks between molecules, not within.

text.text: Iron produced directly from a blast furnace is

body.text: Direct blast-furnace product is pig iron; cast iron is its shaped form, wrought is refined, steel is alloyed.

trap.text: Cast iron tempts as furnace-adjacent, but pig is the direct tap.

text.text: What is the molecular mass of an alkanoic acid, if 0.5 mole of the acid weighs 44g?

key_point.text: Molar mass is mass over moles.

trap.text: 44 answers the sample mass, not per mole — divide by 0.5.

text.text: Alkenes are represented with the general molecular formula

key_point.text: Alkenes carry one double bond: CnH2n.

body.text: Alkanes are +2, alkynes -2. The alcohol formula smuggles oxygen in.

trap.text: CnH2n+2 is the alkane formula — alkenes lose two hydrogens to the double bond.

text.text: The major product when 2-methylpropene reacts with HCl is

key_point.text: Markovnikov puts Cl on the more substituted carbon.

body.text: 2-methylpropene + HCl gives 2-chloro-2-methylpropane. The alternatives place Cl on primary carbons.

trap.text: 1-chloro tempts as end-addition, but the proton goes terminal and Cl goes central.

text.text: In the laboratory preparation of Chlorine, the gas is passed through a wash bottle of water to

key_point.text: The water wash strips HCl mist from chlorine.

body.text: Cl2 preparation carries HCl over; water absorbs it while Cl2 passes. It neither dilutes nor neutralises the product.

trap.text: Dilute tempts, but the wash removes impurity, not strength.

text.text: Carbohydrates can generally be represented by the general formula C\(_x\)(H\(_2\)O)\(_y\), for fructose the value for "X" is

key_point.text: Fructose is a hexose: six carbons.

body.text: C6H12O6, so x = 6. Triose is 3, pentose 5, dodecose 12.

trap.text: 12 doubles to sucrose — fructose alone is six.

text.text: If a gold bar and a silver bar are tied together firmly and left for years, some of the gold particles will be found in the silver bar due to

key_point.text: Solid-state migration over years is diffusion.

body.text: Particles wander down gradients even in solids. Brownian is fluid jitter, osmosis needs a membrane.

trap.text: Brownian tempts on random motion, but years-long metal mixing is bulk diffusion.

text.text: A metal that can be found in the free state in nature is

key_point.text: Unreactive metals occur native; silver is the textbook case here.

body.text: Of the four, silver sits lowest on the reactivity series and is found free. Zinc and iron never are.

trap.text: Copper also occurs native in places — but silver is the least reactive option and the expected answer.

text.text: Which of the following has the highest boiling point?

key_point.text: Hydrogen bonding plus chain length wins boiling points.

body.text: Both alcohols H-bond, but propanol's longer chain adds van der Waals over ethanol. Chloride and hexane cannot H-bond.

trap.text: Hexane tempts as biggest, but H-bonding beats size here.

text.text: From the graph, it can be inferred that
the solubility of X and Y is the same at all temperature
the solubility of X, Y and Z is temperature dependent
solubility of Z increases as temperature increases
solubility of Y increases steadily as temperature increases

key_point.text: Y is the only steadily rising line on the graph.

body.text: From the figure: Y climbs straight with temperature; X curves steeply, Z is flat at 40, Q humps and falls. Same-at-all-temperatures is false everywhere.

trap.text: X tempts as the steepest riser, but the question asks steady increase, which is Y.

text.text: The gas that is commonly used to demonstrate the fountain experiment is

key_point.text: The fountain needs extreme solubility: hydrogen chloride.

body.text: HCl dissolves so fast it collapses the pressure and the water fountains up. The other gases are far less soluble.

trap.text: H2S dissolves, but nowhere near enough to drive the fountain.

text.text: Which of the following statements is false about hard water?
Helps animals to build strong teeth
Cannot be supplied in pipes made of leads
Helps animals to build strong bones.

key_point.text: Hard water CAN run in lead pipes — the scale protects them.

body.text: Dissolved calcium coats lead with scale, blocking dissolution; soft water attacks lead instead. Teeth, bones and taste claims for hard water stand.

trap.text: It reads backwards precisely because soft water is the lead risk, not hard.

text.text: The empirical mass of C\(_6\)H\(_{12}\)O\(_6\) is [H =1, C = 12, O = 16]

body.text: C6H12O6 divides by 6 to CH2O: 12 + 2 + 16 = 30. 180 is the molecular mass.

trap.text: 180 answers the molecular mass, not the empirical one.

text.text: The nitrogenous compound in dead materials in the soil is converted to

body.text: Dead protein breaks down to NH3 first; nitrates come later via nitrifiers.

trap.text: Trioxonitrate(V) is two bacterial steps downstream, not the first product.

text.text: CH\(_3\)C ≡ CCH(CH\(_3\))\(_2\) The IUPAC nomenclature of the compound above is

key_point.text: Longest chain five, triple bond at 2: 4-methylpent-2-yne.

body.text: CH3C.tbd.CCH(CH3)2 numbers to give the triple bond lowest locants; methyl sits on carbon 4.

trap.text: 3-ethyl but-2-yne miscounts the parent chain — five carbons, not four.

text.text: In the laboratory preparation of oxygen using potassium trioxochlorate(V), tetraoxomanganate (VII), usually not recommended in modern laboratory because
it forms explosive mixture with carbonaceous materials

body.text: Potassium trioxochlorate(V) mixtures with fuels or MnO4 residues go off violently — the modern lab avoids the combination.

trap.text: Explosive alone is vague; the carbonaceous-mixture hazard is the specific ban.

text.text: The type of bond between copper(II) tetraamine and chlorine in [Cu(NH\(_3\))\(_4\)]Cl\(_2\)

key_point.text: Complex cation to anion is ionic.

body.text: [Cu(NH3)4]2+ is internally coordinate, but its bond to 2Cl- is electrostatic — ionic.

trap.text: Dative tempts because the complex contains coordinate bonds, but the asked bond is outside the brackets.

text.text: Mg\(_{(s)}\) + 2HCl\(_{(aq)}\) → MgCl\(_2\)\(_{(aq)}\) + H\(_2\)\(_{(g)}\) In the reaction above, magnesium is a reducing agent because

key_point.text: The reducer is the species oxidised.

body.text: Mg 0 to +2 loses electrons — oxidised, so it reduces HCl. Being a metal or solid is incidental.

trap.text: Reduced is the reverse: Mg gains nothing here.

text.text: An example of a physical change is
addition of water to calcium oxide

key_point.text: Dissolving salt is physical — no new substance.

body.text: NaCl in water separates and recrystallises unchanged. Burning, corrosion and CaO hydration all make new compounds.

trap.text: Corrosion tempts as slow, but slow chemistry is still chemistry.

text.text: When a sample of air is passed through alkaline pyrogalol, potash and finally through U-tube containing fused calcium chloride, the components of air left unabsorbed are
noble gases, nitrogen and carbon(IV) oxide

key_point.text: Pyrogalol takes O2, potash takes CO2, CaCl2 takes water.

body.text: Left behind: nitrogen and the noble gases. Each absorber removes exactly one component.

trap.text: Any option keeping CO2 forgets the potash stage.

text.text: An atom of element with the configuration 1S\(^2\)2S\(^2\)2P\(^6\)3S\(^2\)3P\(^5\) is likely to belong to

body.text: 3s2 3p5 totals 7 valence electrons — halogens. Group counts valence, not shells.

trap.text: Group 5 counts only p electrons and forgets the s pair.

text.text: A molecule with a polar covalent bond between atoms exhibits
equal sharing of electron lone pair
unequal sharing of electron lone pair

body.text: Different electronegativities pull the pair off-centre. Equal sharing is non-polar by definition.

trap.text: Lone pairs are uninvolved — polarity is about the bond pair.

text.text: Mg + Pb\(^{2+}\) → Mg\(^{2+}\) + Pb What is the cell notation for the cell reaction above?

key_point.text: Anode left oxidised, cathode right reduced: Mg|Mg2+||Pb2+|Pb.

body.text: Mg oxidises at the anode, Pb2+ reduces at the cathode, salt bridge between. Reversed ion orders break the convention.

trap.text: Option b writes Pb|Pb2+ backwards — oxidised form always trails the bridge.

text.text: The correct arrangement of gases in the order of increasing rate of diffusion is [H = 1, C = 12, N = 14, O = 16, S = 32]

key_point.text: Graham: lightest diffuses fastest, so heaviest leads the slow order.

body.text: M: SO2 64, O2 32, NH3 17, H2 2 — increasing rate is heaviest first: SO2, O2, NH3, H2.

trap.text: Any option leading with CO2 misplaces 44 against 64.

text.text: In a series of solutions with pH of 2.5, 3.5, 7.0 and 8.0, which is likely to turn red moist litmus paper blue?

key_point.text: Only base turns red litmus blue: pH 8.

body.text: 2.5 and 3.5 are acidic, 7.0 neutral. Of the four only 8.0 is alkaline.

trap.text: 7.0 tempts as safe middle, but neutral changes nothing.

text.text: The process by which iron corrodes is

body.text: Hydrated iron(III) oxide formation is rust, specific to iron. Burning, galvanizing and alloying are different processes.

trap.text: Burning is fast oxidation; rusting is the slow aqueous one.

text.text: On heating 12.5g of saturated solution to dryness at 60\(^0\)C, 2g of anhydrous salt was recovered, calculate its solubility in grams per 100g of water.

key_point.text: Solubility is salt per 100 g of water, not solution.

trap.text: 16.0 divides by 12.5 — solution mass instead of water mass.

key_point.text: Alkane plus chlorine in UV light is substitution.

body.text: The figure shows C3H8 + Cl2 giving C3H7Cl + HCl under light — H swapped for Cl. No acid-base, polymer or redox change defines it.

trap.text: Oxidation tempts on Cl2, but the carbon skeleton keeps its oxidation pattern minus one H.

text.text: The gas produced at the cathode during electrolysis of brine is

key_point.text: Cathode reduces cations: brine gives hydrogen.

body.text: H+ discharges over Na+; Cl- goes to the anode. Steam, chlorine and oxygen form elsewhere or never.

trap.text: Chlorine is the anode gas — cathode and anode must not be swapped.

text.text: An example of a salt that can dissolve in water to form a solution with a pH of 7.

key_point.text: Neutral salt from strong acid plus strong base: NaCl.

body.text: NH4Cl and (NH4)2SO4 hydrolyse acidic, Na2CO3 alkaline. Only NaCl holds pH 7.

trap.text: Sodium trioxocarbonate tempts on sodium, but carbonate hydrolyses basic.

text.text: PCl\(_5\)\((_g\)) → PCl\(_3\)\((_s\)) + Cl\(_2\)\((_g\)) In the equation above, the reaction will be spontaneous if

key_point.text: Dissociation grows with heat when Delta H is positive — but of the options, negative Delta H drives spontaneity.

body.text: PCl5 breakdown is endothermic; it runs when entropy wins at high T. Among bare Delta H options, negative is the spontaneity direction.

trap.text: Constant or zero Delta H says nothing about driving force.

text.text: C\(_2\)H\(_5\)OH + CH\(_3\)COOH ⇌ CH\(_3\)COOC\(_2\)H\(_5\) + H\(_2\)O The reaction above is

key_point.text: Acid plus alcohol reversibly is esterification.

body.text: Ethanoic acid + ethanol gives ethyl ethanoate + water. Condensation names the class; esterification names this one.

trap.text: Hydrolysis runs the reverse — ester plus water back to acid and alcohol.

text.text: CH\(_3\) - CH\(_2\) - COOCH\(_2\) - CH\(_3\) From the condensed structure above, the reactants are

key_point.text: Split the ester at the acyl-oxygen bond: propanoic acid + ethanol.

body.text: CH3CH2-COO-CH2CH3 comes from propanoic acid and ethanol. Other pairings misassign carbons to each half.

trap.text: Propanol tempts on three carbons, but the alcohol half here is two.

text.text: The stainless steel alloy is used for making

key_point.text: Stainless cutlery is the everyday alloy use.

body.text: Chromium steel resists rust at the table. Magnets, crushers and bridges use other steels.

trap.text: Bridges use structural steel, not stainless.

text.text: The gas that ammoniacal solution of CuCl\(_2\) is used to absorb from producer or water gas is

body.text: CO complexes with Cu(I) in ammonia — the classic water-gas cleanup. H2, N2 and CO2 pass through.

trap.text: CO2 tempts as acidic gas, but this absorber is CO-specific.

text.text: The liquid state of water at room temperature is as a result of

key_point.text: Liquid water at room temperature needs hydrogen bonding.

body.text: H-bonds between molecules hold water condensed far above its group trend. Covalent and electrovalent bonds are within molecules.

trap.text: Covalent tempts as water's bond, but boiling answers between molecules, not within.

text.text: The source of carbon(II)oxide that acts as air pollutant is

key_point.text: Fuel combustion is the CO source that pollutes.

body.text: Incomplete burning puts CO in exhaust and flue gas. Respiration gives CO2, smog is secondary chemistry, sewage gives methane.

trap.text: Respiration tempts on breathing, but lungs emit CO2, not CO.

text.text: The IUPAC nomenclature of the compound above is

key_point.text: The figure is CH3CH2COO CH2CH3: ethyl propanoate.

body.text: Acid half propanoic (3 C), alcohol half ethyl (2 C): ethyl propanoate. Propyl ethanoate reverses the halves.

trap.text: Propyl ethanoate swaps acid and alcohol halves — count carbons each side of the oxygen.

text.text: If 5g of Iron filling was reacted with excess dilute H\(_2\)SO\(_4\) to evolve hydrogen gas, which came to completion after 10 min, calculate the rate of reaction in g/hr.

key_point.text: Rate is mass over time, scaled to the hour.

body.text: 5 g in 10 min = 0.5 g/min = 30 g/hr.

trap.text: 5 answers grams, not grams per hour — rate needs the time unit.

text.text: The evaluation of petrol from crude oil before it is put on sale is to prevent

key_point.text: Petrol is graded against knock: pinking.

body.text: Octane rating measures anti-knock quality before sale. Reforming, cracking and pyrolysis make petrol; grading prevents pinking.

trap.text: Cracking tempts as refinery work, but evaluation grades, not makes.

text.text: The metal used as a packaging material is

body.text: Light, non-toxic, corrosion-resistant foil. Copper and iron are heavy and reactive; sodium explodes in air.

trap.text: Iron tempts as common metal, but packaging wants lightness plus safety.

key_point.text: V against nT/P is the combined gas law.

body.text: The figure shows volume tracking amount times temperature over pressure — Boyle plus Charles plus Avogadro in one.

trap.text: Boyle alone forgets temperature; Charles alone forgets pressure.

key_point.text: Oxalic acid gives two protons: basicity 2.

body.text: C2H2O4 has two ionisable H. The count is replaceable H, not total atoms.

trap.text: 4 counts every H including non-acidic ones — basicity counts donors only.

text.text: Enzymatic conversion of glucose to ethanol is

key_point.text: Glucose to ethanol by enzyme is fermentation.

body.text: Zymase converts sugar to alcohol plus CO2. Polymerisation joins, hydrogenation adds H2, saponification makes soap.

trap.text: Hydrogenation tempts on -ation endings, but no hydrogen is added here.

text.text: Gold does not require extraction because it is

key_point.text: Gold needs no extraction: free in nature.

body.text: Too unreactive to combine, it sits native. Preciousness is price, not chemistry.

trap.text: Inert is nearly right but vague — free in nature is the extractive fact.

text.text: The process employed in the industrial preparation of tetraoxosulphate(VI) acid is

body.text: V2O5 over SO2 then absorption — the Contact process. Bosch makes ammonia feed, Frasch sulphur, Haber ammonia.

trap.text: Haber tempts as famous-industrial, but Haber is ammonia.

text.text: The catalytic hydrogenation of benzene produces

body.text: Three H2 across three double bonds keeps the ring saturated. Hexane opens the ring; hexene stops halfway.

trap.text: Hexane tempts as saturated, but the ring survives — cyclo stays.

text.text: A by-product of the alkaline hydrolysis of tristearin is a

body.text: Three fatty acids off, propane-1,2,3-triol left — three OH groups. Mono, di, secondary and tertiary misname it.

trap.text: Dihydric counts two where three stand.

text.text: 2SO\(_2\)\(_{(s)}\) + O\(_2\)\(_{(s)}\) ⇌ 2SO\(_3\) ; ΔG° = - ve For the above reaction to be feasible
Sodium in the above reaction is produced by

key_point.text: Fused NaCl electrolysed is the Downs process.

body.text: The figure shows NaCl(l) splitting to Na and Cl2 by electricity — Downs cells. Chlor and Bosch are ammonia; Browning is not a sodium process.

trap.text: Chlor tempts on chlorine product, but the named sodium process is Downs.

text.text: The use of CFCs as a blowing agent has application in

key_point.text: CFC-blown foam is the foam industry.

body.text: Blowing agent expands polymer into foam. Refrigerant and propellant are other CFC uses, not this one.

trap.text: Refrigerant tempts as best-known CFC use, but blowing means foam.

text.text: The metal that will liberate H\(_2\) gas from dilute HNO\(_3\) is

key_point.text: Magnesium frees H2 from dilute nitric acid.

body.text: Mg displaces H+ before HNO3 oxidises further; Cu gives nitrogen oxides instead. Ca is too vigorous, Zn passivates here.

trap.text: Copper tempts as displacer, but nitric acid oxidises copper to NOx, not H2.

text.text: Atom with the electron configuration of 1S\(^2\)2S\(^2\)2P\(^6\)3S\(^2\) belongs to

body.text: Two outer electrons is group II; three shells is period 3 — magnesium. Group counts valence, period counts shells.

trap.text: Group 3 mistakes shell count for valence.

text.text: The relative molecular mass of an alkanoic acid with the empirical formula of CH\(_2\)O is [ H = 1, C = 12, O = 16 ]

key_point.text: Simplest alkanoic fitting CH2O past methanoic is ethanoic: 60.

body.text: HCOOH is 46; CH3COOH is 60. Of the options the intended acid is ethanoic.

trap.text: 46 answers methanoic — the question aims at the two-carbon acid.

text.text: Commercial deodorant is an example of a colloid called

body.text: Liquid droplets in gas is the aerosol colloid. Sols are solid-in-liquid, foams gas-in-liquid, emulsions liquid-in-liquid.

trap.text: Foam tempts on spray texture, but deodorant mist is droplets in air.

text.text: Calculate the time required to liberate 9g of Aluminium metal, when a current of 18A is passed through it. (1F = 96500C , Al = 27)

key_point.text: Faraday with time in minutes: Al needs three faradays.

trap.text: 29.48 minutes forgets the factor of three — Al3+ takes three moles of electrons.

text.text: What is the function of concentrated H\(_2\)SO\(_4\)?
It reacts with metals to give a salt and hydro gas
It produces a cryolite precipitate with basic solution

body.text: It strips water from compounds (sugar to carbon). Salt-plus-hydrogen is dilute-acid behaviour; neutralisation and cryolite are other reagents' jobs.

trap.text: Neutralises alkali is true of any acid — dehydrating is its signature.

body.text: OILRIG: oxidation is loss, reduction is gain. Added, hydrated and hydrolysed describe other processes.

trap.text: Added is reduction — the exact reverse.

text.text: (CH\(_3\))\(_2\)CHCH(OH)CH\(_2\)C(CH\(_3\))\(_3\) The IUPAC name of the compound above is

key_point.text: Longest chain six with OH lowest: 2,5,5-trimethylhexan-3-ol.

body.text: (CH3)2CHCH(OH)CH2C(CH3)3 spans six with OH at 3 and methyls at 2,5,5. Shorter parents miscount.

trap.text: Pentamethylbutanol parents four carbons — the chain is six.

text.text: Anti-freeze used in a vehicle radiator is a mixture of water and

body.text: Propane-1,2,3-triol lowers freezing point. Propanol, propanone and propanal lack the triple-OH colligative punch.

trap.text: Propanol tempts as alcohol, but antifreeze is the triol.

text.text: Magnesium tetraoxosulphate(VI) salt is commonly used as a

body.text: MgSO4 draws water into the bowel. Fertilisers feed plants, disinfectants kill germs, plasticizers soften.

trap.text: Fertiliser tempts on magnesium content, but the medical use is purging.

text.text: The constituents of permalloy are Iron and

body.text: High-permeability Fe-Ni for shielding and transformers. Tin, chromium and copper pair elsewhere.

trap.text: Chromium tempts as stainless partner, but permalloy is Ni.

text.text: An inflated balloon shrinks when placed in a freezer because the
volume of gas increases and expands
gas motion reduces and exert less pressure

key_point.text: Cold slows molecules: less pressure, smaller balloon.

body.text: Kinetic energy falls, collisions soften, volume follows at constant pressure. Molecules neither vanish nor freeze still.

trap.text: Completely stop moving claims absolute zero — a freezer is merely cold.

text.text: The compound in which the oxidation state of nitrogen is + 3 is

key_point.text: N2O3 splits +6 over two nitrogens: +3 each.

body.text: O5 gives +5, O4 gives +4, N2O gives +1. Only N2O3 averages +3.

trap.text: N2O4 tempts on even numbers, but its average is +4.

text.text: Na\(_2\)X ⇌ 2Na\(^+\) + X\(^{2-}\) The bond between Na and X is likely to be

body.text: Metal plus non-metal with full transfer — classic electrovalent. Dative shares, metallic pools, covalent shares equally.

trap.text: Dative tempts on electron-pair talk, but transfer is ionic.

text.text: The compound responsible for the pleasant scent of fruits and perfumes belongs to the class of

body.text: Fruit and perfume scents are volatile esters. Amides, ketones and aldehydes scent differently or not at all.

trap.text: Alkanone tempts on -one endings, but fragrance chemistry is ester chemistry.

text.text: Electron configuration of Chlorine atom is

body.text: 17 electrons fill to 3s2 3p5. Option d scrambles shells; b and c shortchange p.

trap.text: Shell-scrambled options test whether filling order is known, not just totals.

text.text: An importance of solubility is that it
determines the amount of solute that can dissolve in a given amount of solvent
lowers the vapour pressure of the liquid
enables us to know the chemical reactions of the gas with the liquid
raises the boiling point of liquid

body.text: Grams per solvent at saturation — the definition. Vapour, boiling and reaction claims belong elsewhere.

trap.text: Colligative effects tempt, but the importance asked is capacity.

text.text: The disintegration of radioactive phosphorus to silicon follows the first order kinetics with rate constant k\(_1\) = 3.85 x 10\(^{-3}\). Determine the half life of phosphorus.

body.text: t = 0.693/3.85e-3 = 180 s. First order keeps the same half-life throughout.

trap.text: 80 s halves wrong — ln2 is 0.693, not 0.31.

key_point.text: Carbonyl bound to nitrogen is an amide.

body.text: The figure shows R-C(=O)-NH2: alkanamide. Ketones lack N, amines lack the carbonyl, acids lack N.

trap.text: Amine tempts on nitrogen, but carbonyl-plus-nitrogen is amide.

text.text: The fractions of crude oil are best separated by

body.text: Crude fractions separate on a column by boiling range. Steam distillation suits immiscibles; crystallisation and precipitation are not for oils.

trap.text: Steam distillation tempts as distillation, but crude needs fractions.

text.text: In the equation above, the expression for the equilibrium constant, k\(_c\) is

key_point.text: Kc is products over reactants with powers: [X2][Y2]3/[XY3]2.

body.text: From the figure 2XY3 gives X2 + 3Y2: products up, each raised to its coefficient.

trap.text: Option c drops the cubes — coefficients become powers, always.

text.text: How many molecules are there in 4.0 moles of glucose? [Avogadro's number = 6.02 x 10\(^{23}\)]

trap.text: 1.51e23 divides by four instead of multiplying — times, not over.

text.text: Freons pollution in the air are released from

body.text: Aerosol propellants were the dispersive CFC use. Fossil fuel, photosynthesis and decay release other gases.

trap.text: Fossil fuel tempts as pollution, but freons specifically rode aerosols.

text.text: In welding and cutting of metals, the organic gas commonly used in the heating process is

body.text: C2H2 burns hot enough to cut steel. Methane, propene and butane burn cooler.

trap.text: Methane tempts as fuel gas, but welding heat needs acetylene.

body.text: Copper-tin resonance suits music and display. Coins want harder alloys, magnets want iron, aircraft want aluminium.

trap.text: Coins tempts on metal-use, but bronze's voice is musical.

text.text: Find the hydrogen ion, H\(^+\) concentration and hydroxide ion, OH\(^-\) concentration in 0.06 moldm\(^{-3}\) solution of H\(_2\)SO\(_4\).

key_point.text: Diprotic acid doubles H+, water fixes OH-.

trap.text: Halved H+ forgets the second proton — sulphuric gives two.

text.text: After breathing in a test tube that contains acidified K\(_2\)Cr\(_2\)O\(_7\), a man noticed a change in the colour of the acidified K\(_2\)Cr\(_2\)O\(_7\) from orange to green. This suggests the presence of

key_point.text: Orange to green dichromate means alcohol oxidised.

body.text: The breathalyser reaction: ethanol reduces Cr(VI) to Cr(III). Acids, aldehydes and ketones do not flip it this way.

trap.text: Alkanal tempts as oxidisable, but the classic positive is the alcohol.

body.text: The figure lifts A+B at 20 to C+D at 50 over an 80 barrier — heat in. Spontaneous and reversible describe other axes.

trap.text: Reversible tempts on the double hump shape, but energy direction is up.

text.text: The 5\(^{th}\) member of an alkyne series is

key_point.text: Alkynes start at C2, so 5th is C6H10.

body.text: Ethyne C2 is first; fifth is hexyne C6H10 by CnH2n-2. Counting from C1 overshoots into nonexistence.

trap.text: C5H8 counts methane as an alkyne — series starts at ethyne.

What makes it easy to identify a species of birds in the wood?
Flocks of finches could easily become separated
when they get injured by other birds
when they get hungry after being separated from other birds
when they see predators hovering in the sky

In each of the following questions, choose the option that best completes the gap(s). No sooner had Tobi left the house _____ it began to rain.

key_point.text: No sooner pairs only with than.

body.text: No sooner had Tobi left than it began to rain. That and when belong to hardly and scarcely, not to no sooner.

trap.text: When fits scarcely; than is the only partner no sooner takes.

text.text: In each of the following questions, choose the option that best completes the gap(s). What goes around _____ around.

key_point.text: The proverb runs what goes around comes around — singular subject, singular verb.

body.text: What is singular, so the verb is comes. Come breaks concord; is coming and came break the proverb's timeless present.

trap.text: Come looks right beside around but the subject what demands the -s.

text.text: In each of the following questions, choose the option that best completes the gap(s). The boy _____ the flute for about thirty minutes.

key_point.text: For about thirty minutes measures a span up to now — present perfect continuous.

body.text: Has been playing covers the whole thirty minutes to the present. Was playing stops in the past; has play is ungrammatical.

trap.text: Was playing tempts because the scene feels past, but only the perfect reaches back across the full thirty minutes.

text.text: In each of the following questions, choose the option that best completes the gap(s). Each of the answers ______ correct.

key_point.text: Each is always singular, whatever follows of.

body.text: Each of the answers is correct. The plural answers sits inside a prepositional phrase and never governs the verb.

trap.text: Were and are agree with answers, the wrong noun — each governs, not of-phrase contents.

text.text: In each of the following questions, choose the option that best completes the gap(s). Each of the reports ______ been carefully reviewed by the committee

key_point.text: Each takes has; been needs have/has, never is.

body.text: Each of the reports has been reviewed. Each is singular so has; been is a participle and needs an auxiliary, which rules out is alone.

trap.text: Have agrees with reports instead of each; are repeats the error without been.

text.text: In each of the following questions, choose the option that best completes the gap(s). The ____ of armed robbery has been on the increase.

key_point.text: Incidence is the rate of occurrence — what can be on the increase.

body.text: The incidence of armed robbery. An accident or incident is an event; neither can be on the increase, and accidence is a grammar term, not a quantity.

trap.text: Incident names one event where the sentence counts a trend.

text.text: In each of the following questions, choose the option that best completes the gap(s). The doctor ____ him to take his medicine regularly.

key_point.text: Advise is the verb, advice the noun — and the past is wanted.

body.text: The doctor advised him. Adviced is not a word; advise is present; advice names the thing, not the act.

trap.text: Adviced looks like a regular past but the verb advise is already regular without the extra d.

text.text: In each of the following questions, choose the option that best completes the gap(s). He was praised for the ______ achievement.

key_point.text: Laudable means praiseworthy — the only real word of the four.

body.text: He was praised for the laudable achievement. Loudable, loudeble and loudible are built on loud and exist nowhere.

trap.text: The three distractors all echo loud; praise echoes laud.
