This question is based on General Literature Principles and Literary Appreciation. A melodramatic play is based on:
From the diagram above, find the area of the triangle PQR

key_point.text: Split the triangle along the perpendicular.

body.text: The 20 cm side is cut into 11 and 9 by the 13 cm perpendicular, so the area is (1/2)(11)(13) + (1/2)(9)(13) = 71.5 + 58.5 = 130 cm^2.

trap.text: Using the whole 20 cm with the perpendicular once, which reaches 130 by a different route and looks like luck.

key_point.text: A set is unordered, so any rearrangement of the same elements is the same set.

body.text: {4,3,1,5,2} lists exactly the elements 1–5 in a different order, which changes nothing about the set.

trap.text: {1,2,3,4} is missing 5, and listing 5 twice does not add an element — but a well-formed set never repeats.

text.text: Solve the simultaneous equation \(\frac{\text{x}}{2}\) - \(\frac{\text{y}}{5}\) = 1 and y - \(\frac{\text{x}}{3}\) = 8

body.text: From x/2 - y/5 = 1 multiply by 10: 5x - 2y = 10. From y - x/3 = 8 multiply by 3: 3y - x = 24. Eliminating gives x = 6 and y = 10.

trap.text: Eliminating the wrong variable first, or dividing through by a coefficient and losing the constant on the right.

key_point.text: Move the unknowns to one side, remembering the sign flip.

body.text: 2x + 3 > 5x + 8 gives -3x > 5, and dividing by a negative reverses the inequality, so x < -5/3, that is x < -1 2/3.

trap.text: Dividing by -3 and keeping the '<' - the most common inequality slip there is.

text.text: Given that a * b = \(\frac{a + b}{\text{ab}}\) + (a - b). Find the value of 3 * 2

key_point.text: Apply the definition to the pair.

trap.text: Reading ab as a single symbol rather than the product, which turns the first fraction into 5/32.
Taking 125^(-1/3) as 125/3 or forgetting that any non-zero number to the power 0 is 1.

text.text: Find the coordinates of the midpoint of line PQ given P(-3, 4) and Q(5, 6).

trap.text: Averaging the whole pair as one number, or subtracting instead of adding.

text.text: Given that Cos A = \(\frac{12}{13}\) for 0 ≤ A ≤ 90°, find Tan A.

key_point.text: Use the triangle, not a formula.

body.text: cos A = 12/13 gives a 5-12-13 triangle, so sin A = 5/13 and tan A = (5/13)/(12/13) = 5/12.

trap.text: Answering 5/13, which is the sine - the hypotenuse cancels only in the ratio.

text.text: Which of the following angles cannot be constructed using a protractor, a compass, and a sharpened pencil?

key_point.text: Constructible angles come from the standard set.

body.text: 90, 135 and 60 are all standard constructions; 145 is not.

trap.text: Assuming every angle that is a multiple of 5 degrees can be built with a protractor and compass - the protractor is not what is being tested.

text.text: Find the number of permutations of the letters of the word SCHOOL.

body.text: SCHOOL has six letters with O twice, so 6!/2! = 720/2 = 360.

trap.text: Dividing by 2! twice, once per repeated-looking letter, which halves it again.

text.text: Y is partly constant and partly varies as x. When x = 3, y = 7 and when x = 5, y = 11. Find the constants of variation.

body.text: y = a + bx gives b = (11-7)/(5-3) = 2 and a = 7 - 2(3) = 1, so the constants are 1 and 2.

trap.text: Swapping the constants, or taking a as the gradient because 'partly varies' comes first in the sentence.

text.text: The average weight of 15 iron bars is 1000 kg. If the heaviest iron bar is removed, the average weight is reduced by 5 kg. Find the weight in kg of the heaviest iron bar.

key_point.text: Removing the heaviest bar removes one value from the sum.

body.text: 15 bars at 1000 kg gives 15,000 kg. A 5 kg drop over the remaining 14 bars gives 14 x 995 = 13,930, so the heaviest bar is 15,000 - 13,930 = 1070 kg.

trap.text: Applying the 5 kg reduction to the original 15 bars instead of the remaining 14, which changes the answer by 75 kg.

text.text: Find the sum of the entries in the inverse of \(\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 2 \\ 3 & 5 \end{bmatrix}\)

key_point.text: Invert by the adjugate over the determinant.

body.text: The determinant is 1x5 - 2x3 = -1, so the inverse is (1/-1) x [[5,-2],[-3,1]] = [[-5,2],[3,-1]]. The entries sum to -5 + 2 + 3 - 1 = -1.

trap.text: Dividing the adjugate by the matrix instead of by the determinant, or forgetting that 1/-1 = -1.

text.text: A varies directly as b\(^2\) when A = 4, b = 1. Find A when b = 2

key_point.text: Direct variation means the constant is A/b^2.

trap.text: Doubling rather than quadrupling, because b doubles - but the square makes it four times.

text.text: If I is a 2 × 2 identity matrix, find the determinant of the matrix.

key_point.text: The identity's diagonal is all ones.

trap.text: Answering 0, which is the determinant of the zero matrix and the most common guess when the matrix looks too simple.

text.text: The determinant of the matrix \(A = \begin{pmatrix} -2 & 3 & 1 \\ p & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 4 & 2\end{pmatrix}\) is -5. Find the value of p.

key_point.text: Expand along the first row; the top-left minor vanishes.

trap.text: Dropping the sign that flips on every other entry of the expansion, which is what turns -2p + 1 into +2p + 1.

text.text: The mean of the numbers 0, x + 2, 3x + 6, and 4x + 8 is 4, find the value of x.

key_point.text: The mean is 4, so the sum is 4 x 4 = 16.

body.text: The four numbers sum to 0 + (x+2) + (3x+6) + (4x+8) = 8x + 16. Setting 8x + 16 = 16 gives x = 0.

trap.text: Adding the constants before the coefficients, so x = 0 falls out - and 0 is among the options precisely because it is easy to miss.

text.text: Obtain the equation of a straight line passing through (3, 15) whose slope = 3\(\frac{1}{5}\).

key_point.text: Use point-slope, then clear the fraction.

body.text: Slope 3 1/5 = 16/5, so y - 15 = (16/5)(x - 3). Multiplying by 5 and collecting gives 5y - 16x - 27 = 0.

trap.text: Dropping the -3 when clearing the bracket shifts the constant and gives a line through a different point.

text.text: A car dealer bought a used car for ₦270,000 and spent ₦70,000 to refurbish it. He later sold the car for ₦493,000. What was the percentage profit?

body.text: Percentage profit is measured against the **total cost**, which includes the refurbishment: 340,000. 153,000 / 340,000 = 0.45 = 45%.

trap.text: Measuring against the ₦270,000 purchase price alone gives 56.7%, and leaving the refurbishment out of the cost base is the common slip.

key_point.text: Convert every mixed number before touching the expression.

trap.text: Leaving the mixed numbers unconverted is where the fraction usually goes wrong.

text.text: In a basket of fruits, there are 6 grapes, 11 bananas, and 13 oranges. If one fruit is chosen at random, what is the probability that the fruit is either a grape or a banana?

key_point.text: Favourable outcomes are grapes plus bananas.

body.text: 6 + 11 = 17 favourable out of 6 + 11 + 13 = 30 total, giving 17/30.

trap.text: Adding the oranges into the favourable total, or reading 'either' as exclusive-or.

text.text: Calculate the interior angle of a 5 - sided regular polygon

trap.text: 120 is the regular hexagon's angle and 90 the square's - both familiar, neither is the pentagon's.

text.text: A banker spent \(\frac{1}{5}\) of his salary on shirts, \(\frac{1}{3}\) of the remainder on transport, and kept the rest for contingencies. What fraction was left

key_point.text: Each fraction is taken of what is left, not of the salary.

body.text: Shirts take 1/5, leaving 4/5. Transport takes 1/3 of that, 4/15. Left = 4/5 - 4/15 = 8/15.

trap.text: Taking 1/3 of the original salary instead of the remainder gives 7/15.

text.text: Find the probability of getting an even number in a single throw of a six-sided die.

body.text: 2, 4 and 6 out of six equally likely faces give 3/6 = 1/2.

trap.text: Counting 1, 3 and 5 reaches the same answer by the wrong route, which is fine here but not in general.

body.text: x^4 + x^2 + sin x + C, since the integral of 4x^3 is x^4, of 2x is x^2, and of cos x is sin x.

trap.text: The minus on x^2 is the classic slip: it is 2x being integrated, not 2x^2.

key_point.text: A leading minus outside the log flips the whole value.

trap.text: Reading it as log(-0.00001), or dropping the outer minus and answering -5.

text.text: The chord of a circle of radius 17 cm is 30 cm long. Calculate the distance of the chord from the centre of the circle.

key_point.text: The perpendicular from the centre bisects the chord.

body.text: Half the chord is 15, so the distance is the other side of a right triangle: (17^2 - 15^2)^(1/2) = 64^(1/2) = 8.

trap.text: Subtracting 17 - 15 = 2, or forgetting to halve the chord first.

text.text: Find the limit of y = \(\frac{(x^3 - 2x^2 + 6x - 12)}{(x - 2)}\) as x goes to 2.

body.text: x^3 - 2x^2 + 6x - 12 = x^2(x-2) + 6(x-2) = (x-2)(x^2 + 6). The limit as x approaches 2 is therefore 4 + 6 = 10.

trap.text: Direct substitution gives 0/0, which invites the 'Infinity' option - the classic wrong turn on every question of this shape.

text.text: The second and fifth terms of a G.P are 1 and \(\frac{1}{8}\) respectively. Find the common ratio

key_point.text: Divide the fifth term by the second.

trap.text: Taking r^3 = 1/8 and answering r = 1/8 - the cube root is the step being skipped.

text.text: An amount of # 600,000.00 was realized when a principal y was saved for 5% simple interest for 4 years, find the value of y

key_point.text: Simple interest totals in one multiplication.

trap.text: Treating the 5% as compound interest, or dividing by 1.2 in the wrong direction to get the amount rather than the principal.

text.text: Given the progression 3, 5, 7, 9,.... . . . find an expression for the (n - 2)\(^{th}\) term of the progression.

key_point.text: Find the nth term, then substitute n-2.

body.text: The progression is 3, 5, 7, 9 with common difference 2, so T_n = 2n + 1. Putting n - 2: 2(n-2) + 1 = 2n - 3.

trap.text: Substituting n-2 into 2n - 1, which is the term before, not this one.

text.text: Find the derivatives of y = sin 4x

key_point.text: The chain rule multiplies by the derivative of the inside.

body.text: d/dx sin 4x = cos 4x x 4 = 4cos 4x.

trap.text: Giving -4cos x, which drops the 4 from inside the bracket entirely.

text.text: If A = \(\frac{\theta}{360}\)\(\pi r^2\), make \(\theta\) the subject of the formula

body.text: From A = (theta/360) pi r^2, multiplying both sides by 360/(pi r^2) gives theta = 360A/(pi r^2).

trap.text: Leaving theta in the denominator as well as the numerator, which never isolates it.

text.text: What is the minimum value of y = 2 - 4x - 2x\(^2\)

body.text: dy/dx = -4 - 4x = 0 gives x = -1. Substituting: 2 + 4 - 2 = 4.

trap.text: Stopping at the stationary point without evaluating y, or checking only the endpoints and missing the interior minimum.

text.text: If the probability of death is q and the probability of survival is p, find the probability of one death and one survival in an accident involving two persons

key_point.text: One death and one survival can happen in two orders, so the probability is 2pq.

body.text: P(death then survival) = q × p, and P(survival then death) = p × q. Adding the two mutually exclusive cases gives **2pq**.

trap.text: Answering pq counts only one of the two orders and so halves the probability.

text.text: Given the construction in the figure above. What is X\(\hat{Y}\)Z

key_point.text: This is the standard 60 degree construction.

body.text: The arc struck from Y that cuts both arms at the same distance is the first step of constructing an equilateral triangle, whose angles are 60 degrees.

trap.text: Reading the arc as evidence of the angle rather than of the radius - the arc shows equal arms, and the angle follows from the triangle.

key_point.text: Divide by 5 repeatedly, reading the remainders upward.

trap.text: Reading the remainders downward, or forgetting the final quotient of 1 that leads the numeral.

text.text: P is partly constant and varies partly as Q. If P = 32 when Q = 16 and P = 20 when Q = 12, find P when Q = 28

key_point.text: The form is P = a + bQ, whatever 'partly' sounds like.

trap.text: Assuming direct proportionality and scaling 32 by 28/16, which ignores the constant term entirely.

text.text: The word HANDIER can be arranged in how many ways

body.text: HANDIER has seven letters, none repeated, so 7! = 5040.

trap.text: Assuming a repeat exists and halving the factorial for no reason.

text.text: From the table above, estimate the mode of the distribution.

key_point.text: Not yet verifiable from the published figure.

body.text: The mode of a grouped distribution is L + ((f1 - f0) / (2f1 - f0 - f2)) x h, which needs every frequency read exactly. The figure is low-resolution and the frequencies either side of the modal class are not legible with confidence; on the readings we can make, the stored answer does not follow, and on a plausible alternative reading it does. A wrong figure and a wrong answer look identical from here, so we will not guess.

trap.text: Treating a blurred table as a readable one. The modal frequency is easy to spot; the two frequencies beside it are what decide the answer, and those are exactly what the scan loses.

text.text: Find the value of t for which (\(\frac{1}{2}\))\(^{t - 1}\) = 64

key_point.text: Write 64 as a power of one half.

trap.text: Taking 64 as 2^6 and writing t - 1 = 6, which inverts the ratio.

text.text: If 54\(_{ten}\) = X\(_{four}\), find the value of X to 3 decimal point

trap.text: Reading the remainders downward, which yields 213 - the digits in the wrong order.

text.text: Integrate the function y = 3x\(^2\) + 2x - 5 with respect to x.

body.text: x^3 + x^2 - 5x + C, since 3x^2 gives x^3, 2x gives x^2, and -5 stays -5x.

trap.text: Integrating the constant -5 as if it were -5x, or forgetting the constant of integration.

key_point.text: Write the number in standard form, then take the fourth root.

trap.text: Squaring instead of taking the fourth root, which gives 2 x 10^-2 and still looks plausible.

key_point.text: Solve the equation, then read the inequality off it.

body.text: x^2 + 3x - 4 = (x + 4)(x - 1) = 0, so x = -4 or x = 1. The upward parabola lies at or below the axis between them: -4 <= x <= 1.

trap.text: Reversing the interval, or giving the roots as the answer without considering which side the parabola is on.

key_point.text: Simplify each radical to the same surd.

body.text: sqrt 75 = 5sqrt 3, sqrt 12 = 2sqrt 3, sqrt 27 = 3sqrt 3, so the result is (5 - 2 + 3)sqrt 3 = 6sqrt 3.

trap.text: Mis-simplifying sqrt 27 as 2sqrt 3 or 9, either of which changes the total.

text.text: If cos \(\theta\) = \(\frac{\text{x}}{\text{y}}\), find tan \(\theta\) in terms of x and y

key_point.text: Build sin theta from cos theta.

body.text: sin theta = sqrt(1 - x^2/y^2) = sqrt(y^2 - x^2)/y. Then tan = sin/cos = [sqrt(y^2-x^2)/y] / (x/y) = sqrt(y^2 - x^2)/x.

trap.text: Putting y^2 + x^2 under the root, or dividing by cos twice - the cancellation of y is the step that has to happen.

text.text: Given that \(P = \begin{pmatrix} 1 & 3 \\ 2 & -5 \end{pmatrix}\) and Q = \(\begin{pmatrix} 3 & -7 \\ 1 & 2 \end{pmatrix}\) . Find P + 2Q

key_point.text: Scale Q first, then add entry by entry.

trap.text: Adding P and Q first and doubling the sum, which agrees only when P is zero.

text.text: The figure above is a pie chart. Use it to find in degrees those who are doctors

key_point.text: Angle = share of the total x 360.

body.text: The sectors total 16 + 24 + 27 + 21 + 8 = 96. Doctors are 16 of those, so 16/96 x 360 = **60 degrees**.

trap.text: Assuming the sectors total 100 and computing 16 x 3.6 = 57.6, which is offered as 72 only to catch a different slip; the total is 96, not 100.

text.text: In the Venn diagram above, the shaded region is

key_point.text: Read the shading as: inside Q, outside both P and R.

body.text: The shaded part is what belongs to Q alone. Everything inside P or R is excluded, so it is the complement of P u R, taken within Q: **(P u R)' n Q**.

trap.text: (P n Q)' n R reads as the complement of the P-Q overlap, which shades a different region entirely.

text.text: The table above shows the weights of twelve mathematics students. Find the modal weight.

key_point.text: Not yet verifiable from the published figure.

body.text: The modal weight depends on the frequencies in the table, and the scan is too low-resolution to read them with confidence. On our reading the frequencies do not support the stored answer; on a different reading they might. We will not publish a claim about the arithmetic of a figure we cannot read, and we will not redraw a table that came from a source we do not control.

trap.text: Verifying a statistics question from a table you cannot actually resolve. Both the answer and the criticism of it depend on digits nobody has read properly.

text.text: A binary operation * is defined on the set X = {1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6} as a*b = ab + a + b. Compute 1 * 3

trap.text: Multiplying only the two arguments and forgetting the two extra terms, which gives 3.

text.text: From the table above, determine the upper - class boundary of the modal class

key_point.text: The modal class is the one with the highest frequency; its upper class boundary is half a unit above the class limit.

body.text: The highest frequency is 10, in the class 21-30. In a grouped distribution the classes run 20.5-30.5, so the **upper class boundary is 30.5**.

trap.text: Answering 30, the class limit rather than the class boundary - the half-unit correction exists precisely because the data are continuous.

text.text: A bird flies from a tree P on a bearing of N60° E to a building, Q, a distance of 200 km. It then changes course and flies to another tree R on a bearing of S30°E. Tree R is directly east of tree P. Calculate the distance of the building to tree R.

body.text: P to Q on N60E puts Q at (200 sin 60, 200 cos 60) = (173.2, 100). From Q on S30E the drop of 100 needs d cos 60 = 100, giving d = 200.

trap.text: Reading S30E as 30 east of south when the perpendicular is required, which changes the value.

text.text: Given the triangle XYZ above, calculate the value of Cot \(\theta\) and the length XY, respectively

body.text: XY = sqrt(13^2 - 11^2) = sqrt 48. At X, cot theta is adjacent over opposite = XY/YZ = sqrt 48 / 11.

trap.text: Taking cot as opposite over adjacent, or reading the 11 cm as the hypotenuse when the 13 cm already is.

text.text: Which of these colours in the visible spectrum has the longest wavelength?

key_point.text: Red sits at the long-wavelength end of the visible spectrum (~700 nm).

body.text: Wavelength grows violet to red across VIBGYOR; red is the last colour before infrared. Violet is shortest, not longest.

trap.text: Violet is the highest-frequency colour — frequency and wavelength run opposite, and the question asks wavelength.

text.text: The power of a lens in diopters is

key_point.text: Lens power in diopters is the reciprocal of focal length in metres.

body.text: P = \(\frac{1}{\text{f}}\). A 1 m focal length is 1 diopter; shorter focus means a stronger lens.

trap.text: 3f and 2f read like formulas, but power is an inverse, not a multiple.

text.text: A man moves 6.0m East and then 10.0m N30°E. How far is he from his starting point?

key_point.text: Resolve N30°E into components, then recombine.

trap.text: Adding 6.0 and 10.0 directly ignores direction — displacement is the vector sum of components, not the arithmetic sum of legs.

text.text: The density of water is 1g/cm\(^3\) while that of ice is 0.9g/cm\(^3\). Calculate the change in volume when 90g of ice is completely melted.

key_point.text: Mass is conserved; volume follows density on each side.

body.text: V_ice = 90/0.9 = 100 cm\(^3\); V_water = 90/1.0 = 90 cm\(^3\). Change = 100 − 90 = 10 cm\(^3\) — the melt contracts.

trap.text: 90 cm\(^3\) answers the water's volume, not the change — read what shrinks.

text.text: According to the kinetic theory of gases, the pressure exerted by a gas on the walls equals.
Momentum imparted to the walls per unit area.
Change in momentum per unit volume.
Change in momentum imparted to the walls per unit area.
Rate of change of momentum imparted to the walls per second per unit area.

key_point.text: Pressure is force per area; force is rate of change of momentum.

body.text: Gas pressure on a wall is the momentum the molecules hand over per second, per unit area — dp/dt per area.

trap.text: Change of momentum without the rate (per second) is impulse, not pressure.

text.text: Which of the following is not true about a wave in a plucked string?

key_point.text: A plucked string vibrates across its length — transverse.

body.text: Mechanical (needs the string) ✓, crest ✓, transverse ✓. Longitudinal oscillation along the string is what a plucked string never does.

trap.text: Sound waves are longitudinal — but the wave asked about is in the string, not the air.

text.text: The emf of a cell is the potential difference across its terminals when it is in

key_point.text: Emf is the terminal p.d. with no current flowing.

body.text: A cell shows its full emf only in an open circuit; any closed loop drops volts across internal resistance.

trap.text: Closed circuit reads terminal p.d. under load — always less than emf.

text.text: The thermometric property of mercury is best on the change in

key_point.text: A mercury thermometer reads the liquid's volume change.

body.text: Mercury expands uniformly with temperature; the thread length tracks volume. Density, pressure and resistance belong to other thermometers.

trap.text: Resistance belongs to platinum thermometers, not mercury.

text.text: Some of the features of the human eye that greatly help to refract light entering the eyes are

key_point.text: The cornea does most of the bending; the lens fine-tunes.

body.text: Both refract. The aqueous and vitreous humors transmit and support — they are not the refracting elements.

trap.text: Every option pairs two real eye parts; only cornea and lens both refract.

text.text: When both the object and its image move together in the same direction relative to the observer, then there is

key_point.text: Parallax vanishes when object and image share the motion.

body.text: Parallax error is relative shift against a background. Moving together, object and image keep station — no error.

trap.text: Blurred image is an optics failure, not a parallax outcome.

text.text: The diagram above shows a magnetic field due to a

key_point.text: Concentric circles around a straight wire: current-carrying straight conductor.

body.text: The figure shows circular field lines centred on the straight conductor with current out of the page — the textbook straight-wire pattern. Solenoid and coil fields run through loops, not around a bare wire.

trap.text: A circular coil also makes circles — but centred on the loop's axis through rings, not on a straight wire.

text.text: I. The colour of light depends on its frequency II. When white light is dispersed by a triangular prism, yellow is deviated more than green III. Rainbows are formed when rains fall heavily. Which of the above statements is/are correct about dispersion and colours?

key_point.text: Colour follows frequency; deviation grows with it.

body.text: I holds (colour↔frequency). II reverses the prism: green outranks yellow in frequency, so green deviates more. III invents meteorology — rainbows need sun behind rain at 42°, not heavy rain.

trap.text: Yellow-deviated-more sounds plausible until frequency order is written out: red, then yellow, then green, then blue.

text.text: A Force 18 N pulls a 40 kg mass on a horizontal floor at 0.3 ms\(^{-2}\). Find the coefficient of friction.

key_point.text: Friction is what remains after ma is accounted for.

body.text: ma = 40×0.3 = 12 N of the 18 N accelerates; 6 N fights friction. μ = 6/(40×10) = 0.015.

trap.text: 0.300 copies the acceleration straight across — μ is a ratio, never an acceleration.

text.text: A 500W electric oven plugged into a 220 V source will consume an electric current of

trap.text: 220/500 inverts the ratio — current comes from dividing power by the supply, not the reverse.

text.text: A hydraulic press consists of two cylinders of cross-sectional radius r\(_1\) and r\(_2\). If a force of 200N applied to the smaller piston (r\(_1\)), causes a force of 3200N to be transmitted onto the larger piston (r\(_2\)). The ratio r\(_1\): r\(_2\) is?

key_point.text: Force ratio is area ratio is radius-squared ratio.

body.text: F∝A∝r², so (r₁/r₂)² = 200/3200 = 1/16 and r₁:r₂ = 1:4.

trap.text: 1:16 answers the area ratio — radii need the square root.

text.text: The gravitational pull between two bodies is 20N. Find the gravitational pull when their distance of separation is doubled.

key_point.text: Gravity falls as the square of distance.

body.text: Doubling r quarters F: 20/4 = 5 N.

trap.text: 10 N halves instead of quartering — inverse square, not inverse.

text.text: The volume of a 1 cm\(^3\) metal ball increases by 0.0018 cm\(^3\) when heated through temperature θ. If the linear expansivity of the ball is 2.0 x 10\(^{-5} K^{-1}\), find θ.

key_point.text: Volume expansivity is three times linear.

trap.text: Using α un-tripled gives 90 — volume needs β, three times α.

text.text: For a gas, which pair of variables is inversely proportional to each other (provided other conditions are constant), where P = pressure, T= temperature, V= volume, and n= number of molecules?

key_point.text: Boyle's law: pressure trades against volume at fixed temperature.

body.text: P∝1/V with T constant. The other pairs rise together or need more held constant.

trap.text: P,T rise together (pressure law) — the inverse pair is Boyle's.

text.text: A boy uses a single string pulley system to lift a mass of 20kg moving with a velocity of 5ms\(^{-1}\). What is the power developed by the boy if g = 10ms\(^{-2}\)?

key_point.text: Power is force times velocity; the force here is weight.

trap.text: 100 W divides by g twice — weight already contains g.

text.text: Without considering the containing vessel, what mass of boiled water can raise the temperature of 8 kg of water from 25°C to 60°C when mixed in a heat-proof container?

key_point.text: Heat lost equals heat gained; boiled means 100°C.

body.text: m×c×(100−60) = 8×c×(60−25) → 40m = 280 → m = 7 kg. c cancels throughout.

trap.text: Mixing from 25 needs the cold side's rise (35), not 60 — gains and losses anchor on different ends.

text.text: Which of the following has the least thermal conductivity?

key_point.text: Gases conduct worst; still air is the insulator everything copies.

body.text: Air ≈ 0.026 W/m·K — far below glass, water and ash. Double glazing works by trapping it.

trap.text: Water feels cold to touch, but touch measures heat flow from skin, not the conductivity ranking.

text.text: 5400kJ of heat energy was lost when some amount of steam condensed to water for drinking purposes at 15° C. What is the quantity of water collected? [L\(_f \) = 2.26 × 10\(^6\) Jkg\(^{-1}\), c\(_w\) = 4200 Jkg\(^{-1}K^{-1}\)]

key_point.text: Condensing steam pays latent heat, then the water cools.

trap.text: 1.84 kg counts only the latent heat and forgets the cooling from 100 to 15.

text.text: Charge carriers in doped semiconductors are

key_point.text: Doping donates electrons or accepts them, leaving holes.

body.text: n-type carries extra electrons, p-type carries holes. Protons and neutrons never leave the nucleus; ions belong to chemistry.

trap.text: Anions and cations are chemistry's carriers — semiconductors speak electrons and holes.

text.text: If the critical angle for a glass–air boundary is 45°, what is the refractive index of the glass?

key_point.text: Refractive index is one over sine of the critical angle.

trap.text: 2√2 doubles instead of inverting — the reciprocal is the whole formula.

text.text: The volume of a fixed mass of gas at 0° C is 200 m\(^3\). What is its volume at 273° C at constant pressure?

key_point.text: Charles's law needs kelvin, and 0°C is 273 K.

body.text: V₂ = 200×546/273 = 400 m\(^3\). Celsius ratios would divide by zero — the law runs on absolute temperature.

trap.text: 800 doubles by doubling Celsius — temperature ratios only work in kelvin.

text.text: The device that operates using the magnetic effect of electric current is

key_point.text: The bell's hammer is thrown by an electromagnet.

body.text: Current magnetises the core, the armature snaps across, the circuit breaks, the spring returns it — buzz. Rheostats vary resistance; thermostats sense heat; microphones sense sound.

trap.text: Thermostat has thermo in the name but works by expansion, not magnetism.

text.text: Calculate the decay constant of a radioactive isotope of half-life 138.5 s.

key_point.text: Decay constant is ln2 over half-life.

trap.text: Using log₁₀ instead of ln, or plain 1/138.5, lands among the distractors.

text.text: How long will it take to heat 4 kg of water from 30°C to 65°C using an electric kettle taking 5 A from a 240 V supply? (Specific heat capacity of water = 4200 J kg\(^{-1}\) K\(^{-1}\))

key_point.text: Electrical energy in equals heat gained.

trap.text: Halving ΔT or doubling power gives 245 — energy bookkeeping has one answer.

text.text: The figure shows a uniform metre rule of weight 100 N balanced by a knife edge at the 10 cm mark and a cord attached at the 85 cm mark. What is the tension in the string?

key_point.text: Moments about the pivot balance; the weight acts at the rule's midpoint.

body.text: 100 N at 50 cm pulls 40 cm right of the 10 cm pivot: 4000 N·cm clockwise. The cord at 85 cm pulls 75 cm right: T = 4000/75 ≈ 53.33 N. The figure confirms the layout; the numbers decide it.

trap.text: Moments about the rule's end give the wrong fulcrum — the pivot, not the end, balances.

text.text: What form of energy is present in the food we eat?

body.text: The body runs on chemistry: bonds broken and remade release energy. Kinetic, mechanical and potential describe motion and position, not what food holds.

trap.text: Mechanical sounds physical, but food's energy is locked in molecules until digestion frees it.

text.text: What magnitude of electric current can store 2.5 J of energy in a 3 H induction coil?

key_point.text: Coil energy is half L I squared — solve for current.

trap.text: 5.00 A forgets the half; energy scales with current squared, not linearly.

text.text: A machine has an efficiency of 80%. If the input work is 200J, the output work is?

key_point.text: Efficiency is output over input — output is always less.

body.text: Output = 0.80 × 200 = 160 J. No machine returns more than it takes.

trap.text: 250 J inverts the ratio (200/0.8) — efficiency below 100% shrinks, never grows.

text.text: A wooden block of relative density 0.4 floats in a liquid of density 1600 kg m\(^{-3}\). What fraction of its volume is immersed?

key_point.text: Fraction immersed equals relative density over fluid density.

trap.text: 0.15 and 0.10 invent densities the stem never states — one ratio decides it.

text.text: Lining the walls of an auditorium with perforated materials reduces

key_point.text: Soft perforated linings kill echoes — reverberation.

body.text: Reverberation is sound lingering by reflection; absorbent walls shorten it. Diffraction bends, refraction transmits, and auditorium pulse is not a phenomenon.

trap.text: Diffraction tempts because perforations look wave-like, but the linings absorb rather than bend.

text.text: If an object sinks in water, it means that
Its density is greater than that of water
its density is less than that of water
water pressure is greater than its weight

key_point.text: Sinking means denser than the fluid.

body.text: Weight beats upthrust exactly when body density exceeds fluid density. Equal means floating at the surface, not sinking.

trap.text: Upthrust-equals-weight describes floating equilibrium — the opposite outcome.

text.text: A well-lagged thin metal rod of length 0.2 m has a temperature gradient of 416 K m\(^{-1}\). If one end is at 233° C, what is the temperature at the other end?

key_point.text: Temperature drop is gradient times length.

body.text: ΔT = 416 × 0.2 = 83.2 K, so the far end sits near 233 + 83.2 ≈ 316.2°C against option 316.28°C (source rounding).

trap.text: 141.20°C subtracts a gradient ten times too large — length is 0.2 m, not 2 m.

text.text: The movement of particles in liquids and gases is referred to as

key_point.text: Random particle motion in fluids is Brownian motion.

body.text: Liquids and gases show the jitter Brown saw in pollen grains. Translational and vibrational describe how molecules move in principle; Brownian names the observed random walk.

trap.text: Vibrational belongs to solids locked in lattices, not to fluids.

text.text: What mass of silver is deposited during electrolysis when a current of 0.8 A flows for 25 minutes?

key_point.text: Faraday's law: mass equals electrochemical equivalent times charge.

trap.text: Forgetting minutes-to-seconds (×60) collapses the charge and the mass with it.

text.text: The thermal capacity of a body depends on one of the following

key_point.text: Thermal capacity is mass times specific capacity — nature and mass.

body.text: C = mc: it scales with how much stuff and what stuff. Heat quantity is what it stores, not what fixes it.

trap.text: Quantity of heat confuses the content with the container — capacity is per-degree by definition.

text.text: What is the pressure exerted by 4.5m\(^3\) of gas at 17°C in a cylinder if the number of moles is 8.3 moles? (R = 8.31 JK\(^{-1}\)mol\(^{-1}\))

key_point.text: Ideal gas law in kelvin: temperature is 290 K, not 17.

trap.text: Using 17°C raw gives a pressure thirty times too small — gas laws run on absolute temperature.

text.text: The tangential force acting on an object that opposes it from sliding freely on the adjacent surface is called

key_point.text: The tangential resistance to sliding is frictional force.

body.text: It acts along the surfaces, opposing relative motion. Weight pulls down, upthrust pushes up, normal pushes across — none acts tangentially against sliding.

trap.text: Normal force is perpendicular to the surfaces; friction is the parallel one.

text.text: The point where no magnetic effect is felt around a magnet is

key_point.text: Field lines never cross there — the neutral point.

body.text: Where a magnet's field cancels (against Earth's, typically), a compass feels nothing. Near, far and infinite points all still sit in the field.

trap.text: Far point weakens the field but never zeroes it — only cancellation does that.

text.text: If the specific gravity of a liquid is 0.76, calculate its density((\(\rho_w\) = 1000Kgm\(^{-3}\))

key_point.text: Specific gravity times water's density, units carried along.

trap.text: 76 and 7.6 drop factors of ten — specific gravity multiplies, and the units ride with the thousand.

text.text: Copper of 0.2g and silver of 1.2g are deposited when current is passed through copper and silver voltameter. Calculate the electrochemical equivalent, Z of silver if that of copper is 0.00028gC\(^{-1}\)

key_point.text: Faraday's second law: same charge, masses in electrochemical ratio.

trap.text: Dividing the masses the wrong way inverts six into a sixth.

text.text: Calculate the heat capacity of a material that absorbs 48KJ of heat at a differential temperature of 53°C

key_point.text: Heat capacity is heat over temperature change.

trap.text: Dividing by 53°C needs the differential as stated — 48 kJ is 48,000 J, not 48.

text.text: Which of the following electromagnetic spectra has the shortest wavelength?

key_point.text: X-rays sit below ultraviolet — shorter wavelength, higher energy.

body.text: Order runs radio, micro, infrared, visible, ultraviolet, X-rays, gamma. Of the four listed, X-rays are shortest.

trap.text: Ultraviolet tempts as exotic, but X sits a full band beyond it.

text.text: A wire of radius 0.3cm is used to lift a block of 1.5kg. Calculate the stress introduced into the wire [ take g = 10m/s\(^2\)]

key_point.text: Stress is force over true area — radius in metres first.

trap.text: Centimetres unconverted inflate the area ten-thousandfold — 0.3 cm is 0.003 m before anything else.

text.text: The quantity of heat required to convert 5kg of ice at its melting point to water without a change of temperature is

key_point.text: Melting at constant temperature is latent heat of fusion.

body.text: The 5 kg is already liquid-bound; the named quantity is latent heat. Specific latent heat is per kilogram — the question asks for the quantity itself.

trap.text: Specific heat capacity warms without change of state; nothing here changes temperature.

text.text: Which of the following is better for measuring a very small resistance?

key_point.text: Null methods measure small resistances — Wheatstone bridge.

body.text: The bridge balances to zero, so lead and contact resistances drop out. Voltmeters read p.d., rheostats vary it, potentiometers compare emfs.

trap.text: Potentiometer tempts on precision reputation, but its job is emf comparison, not resistance.

text.text: In an A.C circuit, the instantaneous current is 7A. What is the root mean square(r.m.s) value of the current I\(_{r.m.s}\)

key_point.text: Rms is peak over root two — 7 A here is the maximum.

body.text: Irms = 7/√2 ≈ 4.95 ≈ 5 A. (Instantaneous strictly varies; the JAMB reading takes 7 A as the peak.)

trap.text: Treating 7 A as already-rms answers the question it did not ask.

text.text: Calculate the depth of a swimming pool if the apparent depth is 10cm(refractive index of water is 1.33)

key_point.text: Real depth is index times apparent depth.

body.text: n = real/apparent, so real = 1.33 × 10 = 13.3 cm. The pool is deeper than it looks.

trap.text: 7.5 cm divides instead of multiplying — the real thing exceeds the appearance, never the reverse.

text.text: A 5 \(\mu\) positively charged particle is moving at 45° to the direction of magnetic field with 3 x 10\(^4\)m/s speed. If it experiences a force of 6N, what is the value of the flux density of the field?

key_point.text: Magnetic force is qvB sinθ — solve for B.

trap.text: Dropping sin45° answers a perpendicular entry the stem never states.

text.text: The dimensional symbol of tension in a string is expressed as

key_point.text: Tension is a force: mass, length, inverse time squared.

body.text: [T] = MLT\(^{-2}\). Forces always carry M¹L¹T⁻² regardless of the string.

trap.text: MLT² forgets the inverse square — dimensions of force never carry positive time.

text.text: From the above circuit, calculate the impedance ((\(\pi\) = \(\frac{22}{7}\), f = 50Hz)

key_point.text: Series impedance adds resistance and reactance in quadrature.

trap.text: Adding 45 and 157 directly forgets quadrature — resistance and reactance are perpendicular, combined by Pythagoras.

text.text: What pressure would a 5000N weight of water exert at the bottom of a reservoir containing it if its length and breadth are 10m and 5m, respectively

key_point.text: Pressure is weight over base area.

body.text: P = 5000/(10×5) = 100 Pa. Depth and volume never enter — the weight and footprint decide it.

trap.text: Bringing in depth confuses hydrostatic ρgh with a straight weight-over-area.

text.text: Waves that vibrate in a vertical plane(standing upright)
The motion of the source toward the observer
The motion of the source away from the observer
waves that reflect off a boundary and interfere with themselves

key_point.text: Standing waves are interference with their own reflection.

body.text: A wave bouncing off a boundary superposes on itself — nodes and antinodes, no travel. Source motion makes Doppler shifts, not standing waves.

trap.text: A vertically vibrating source still launches travelling waves; standing needs the return trip.

text.text: From the above figure, a uniform meter rule is suspended by two cords from a height. Calculate T?
From the diagram above, the sine of the angle of refraction in glass is

key_point.text: Snell from the normal: sine of r is sine of i over n.

body.text: The figure gives i = 30° from the normal into n = 1.5 glass. sin r = sin30°/1.5 = 0.5/1.5 ≈ 0.33 → 0.3.

trap.text: 0.4 inverts the ratio the wrong way — refraction into denser glass shrinks the sine, and 0.5/1.5 is one third.

text.text: What happens to the speed of sound in air when the pressure increases at a constant temperature

key_point.text: Sound speed in a gas depends on temperature, not pressure.

body.text: v = √(γRT/M): at constant T every term is fixed, so pressure changes nothing. Squeeze the air and the wave keeps its pace.

trap.text: Increase feels right because pressure sounds like pushing — but the formula has no P in it at fixed T.

text.text: The operation of a photovoltaic cell is possible by the action of

key_point.text: Photovoltaic action is a semiconductor effect.

body.text: Light frees charge carriers across a band gap — a semiconductor property. Conductors have no gap to cross, insulators too wide a one, chemistry describes batteries, not photocells.

trap.text: Chemical tempts because batteries are chemical — but a photocell converts light, not reagents.

text.text: A concave mirror of focal length 20cm produces an erect image that is four times the object, the object distance from the mirror is

key_point.text: Erect and magnified in a concave mirror means inside the focus.

body.text: A concave mirror magnifies erect only for objects within F: u < 20 cm (indeed u = 15 cm for m = 4). Beyond F the image inverts.

trap.text: Beyond-20 cm options describe real inverted images — erect rules them all out at once.

text.text: The resultant of the force shown above is

key_point.text: Resultant is the vector sum: 3 N up against 4 N across.

body.text: From the figure: vertical 15 − 12 = 3 N up; horizontal 8 − 4 = 4 N right. R = √(9 + 16) = 5 N.

trap.text: 18.00 N adds magnitudes ignoring direction — vectors add by components, never by arithmetic.

text.text: A circular parallel plate capacitor with radius 6cm is separated by 0.12cm. Calculate the capacitance of the capacitor [\(\pi\) = 3.142, ε\(_0\) = 8.85 x 10\(^{-12}\)Nm\(^2\)C\(^2\)]

key_point.text: Capacitance scales with area over separation.

trap.text: 5.1×10\(^{11}\) F inverts the tiny scale — a centimetre capacitor stores picofarads, never hundreds of farads.

text.text: Calculate the specific heat capacity of a metal rod of mass 0.025kg whose temperature was raised by 15°C when 1000J of heat energy was added to the rod(assuming the heat loss to the surrounding is negligible)

key_point.text: Specific capacity is heat over mass times rise.

trap.text: Forgetting kilograms (0.025, not 25) inflates the answer a thousandfold.

text.text: The speed of sound in air is 60 m/s. How far from the centre of a storm is an observer who hears a thunder clap 4s after the flash of the lightning?

key_point.text: Distance is speed times delay — at the stipulated speed.

body.text: d = 60 × 4 = 240 m. (Real thunder runs ~340 m/s; the stem stipulates 60 and the key follows the stipulation.)

trap.text: 340 m answers the real world instead of the question asked — follow the stem's number.

text.text: Which of the following thermometer types best responds to a change in temperature

key_point.text: Resistance thermometers respond fastest and most steadily.

body.text: Platinum resistance tracks temperature with barely any lag. Liquid-in-glass (mercury, alcohol) is slow; gas thermometers are bulky standards.

trap.text: Gas thermometer tempts on accuracy reputation, but best response means speed plus steadiness.

text.text: A 25cm long pinhole camera produces a one-fifth of an object's size. Calculate the object distance

key_point.text: Magnification is image distance over object distance.

body.text: 1/5 = 0.25/u gives u = 1.25 m. The 25 cm camera length is the image distance.

trap.text: Inverting the ratio (5 × 0.25) answers a five-times enlargement — the image is one fifth, not five times.

text.text: What is the mass of a particle with speed 2.7 x 10\(^8\)m/s and wavelength 4.0 x 10\(^{-7}\)mm? (h = 6.63 x 10\(^{-34}\)Js)
At what distance from a 1.2 x 10\(^{-7}\)C point charge will the electric field intensity be equal to 4.8 x 10\(^{-4}\)NC\(^{-1}\) [ Take \(\frac{1}{4\pi ε_0}\) = 9.0 x 10\(^9\)]

key_point.text: Field falls as distance squared — solve the square root.

trap.text: Forgetting the root answers millions of metres — field laws need the square root undone.

text.text: Using the oscillating simple pendulum above, the maximum kinetic energy is obtained at

key_point.text: Kinetic energy peaks where speed peaks: the lowest point.

body.text: The figure labels the bottom Q (control point) between extremes P and S. Maximum speed — hence maximum KE — is at Q.

trap.text: P and S are the turning points: momentarily at rest, all energy potential.

text.text: A collection of condensed suspended dust particles in the air constitute

key_point.text: Suspended dust thick enough to see through is fog.

body.text: Fog is cloud at ground level. Mist is thinner, cloud is aloft, rain falls.

trap.text: Cloud tempts on composition, but suspended dust at breathing height is fog by definition.

text.text: A body is moving initially at 4m/s. If it's impulse after accelerating at 5m/s\(^2\) for 2s is 60Kgms\(^{-1}\). What is its mass?

key_point.text: Impulse is the change in momentum — solve for mass.

trap.text: Using final momentum alone (14m = 60) forgets the 4 m/s head start — impulse is the change.

text.text: A bore made in an aluminium block at 34°C is 3.48cm\(^3\). What is the new bore when the temperature was raised to 340°C [α\(_a\) = 24 x 10\(^{-6}\)K\(^{-1}\)]

key_point.text: A hole expands as if filled with the same material.

trap.text: Using α un-tripled answers two-thirds of the growth — cavities need volume expansivity.

text.text: A short-sighted person's far point is 95cm. The defect can be corrected using
Plano convex lens of focal length 90cm

key_point.text: Short sight needs a diverging lens of the far-point focal length.

body.text: A 95 cm far point wants a concave lens of f = 95 cm spreading parallel light as if from 95 cm. Mirrors never correct refraction errors; converging lenses fix long sight.

trap.text: Diverging mirror borrows the right word for the wrong device — correction is lenses, not mirrors.

text.text: A refrigerator uses 150W. If it is kept on for 336 hours nonstop. What is the energy consumed in Kwh?

trap.text: 150 × 336 in watts gives watt-hours — the kilo prefix must divide by a thousand.

text.text: The commonly used materials for shielding or screening magnetism is

key_point.text: High-permeability soft iron channels field lines away.

body.text: Shielding works by giving flux an easy path around the region. Aluminium, brass and copper are near-air magnetically.

trap.text: Copper tempts on conductivity, but shielding is about permeability, not conduction.

text.text: One of the following is not a radiation detector

key_point.text: The odd one out produces charge instead of detecting radiation.

body.text: Scintillation chambers, Geiger–Muller counters and film badges all register radiation. The electrophorus generates charge by induction.

trap.text: Film badge tempts as passive, but passive recording is still detection.

text.text: What is the electrolyte used in wet Leclanche cell

key_point.text: The wet Leclanché cell breathes ammonium chloride.

body.text: NH₄Cl paste is the classic depolariser-electrolyte. Lead dioxide belongs to accumulators, nickel hydroxide to NiCd.

trap.text: Lead dioxide borrows from the car battery — a different chemistry entirely.

text.text: In electromagnetic induction, the generated electricity is actually a voltage called

key_point.text: Generated voltage has one name: induced emf.

body.text: Faraday's product is an emf whether it drives current or not. Eddy currents are a special case; watts are power.

trap.text: Eddy current names currents in bulk metal — the voltage itself is emf.

text.text: Which of the following is a basic Unit?

key_point.text: SI base quantities are seven — current among them.

body.text: Ampere is base; joule, volt and ohm all derive from it (with kg, m, s).

trap.text: Volt tempts as fundamental because it feels basic — it is kg·m²·s⁻³·A⁻¹, fully derived.

text.text: The acceleration of the body given above ( upthrust = 10N)

key_point.text: Net force is weight minus the two upward pulls.

body.text: From the figure: weight 10×10 = 100 N down; upthrust 10 N and drag 15 N up. F = 100 − 25 = 75 N down; a = 75/10 = 7.5 m/s².

trap.text: Counting only upthrust forgets the drag arrow — every upward pull comes off the weight.

text.text: The distance between two successive trough points of a wave is

key_point.text: Trough to trough is one full cycle — one wavelength.

body.text: Periodicity defines it: the pattern repeats every λ, troughs included.

trap.text: Half wavelength separates trough from crest — same-side points take the whole.

text.text: What colour has the lowest frequency in the spectrum of white light?

key_point.text: Lowest frequency is the reddest light.

body.text: Frequency climbs violet-ward; red sits lowest. Yellow, indigo and blue all oscillate faster.

trap.text: Blue tempts as calm-looking, but frequency is physics, not mood.

text.text: If 10 objects, tinsels are placed between the mirror of a Kaleidoscope with an inclination of 30°, how many images are formed?

key_point.text: Each object makes 360/θ − 1 images; ten objects make ten times that.

body.text: 360/30 − 1 = 11 per object; 10 × 11 = 110. Tinsels just multiply the count.

trap.text: Forgetting the minus one counts the object itself as its own image.

text.text: When capacitors are connected in series across a potential difference, there is a loss in their stored energy because:
Increase in the internal resistance of the voltage
Unequal charges being deposited on the capacitors
a charge flows between the capacitors
decrease in the overall capacitance of the capacitors

key_point.text: Series connection shrinks total capacitance — and stored energy with it.

body.text: 1/C falls below every member, so ½CV² at the same V falls too. Charge is equalised, not lost between plates.

trap.text: Charge flowing between capacitors sounds like loss, but series charge equalises by induction without leaving.

text.text: Two identical cells, each of emf 1.5V and internal resistance 1\(\Omega\), are connected in parallel to supply current to a 2 \(\Omega\) resistor. What is the total current

key_point.text: Parallel cells share voltage and halve resistance.

body.text: Equivalent: 1.5 V with 0.5 Ω internal. Total 2.5 Ω against 2 Ω load: I = 1.5/2.5 = 0.6 A.

trap.text: Adding the emfs (3 V) wires them in series — parallel keeps 1.5 V.

text.text: The focal length of the natural eye lens is variable due to the action of the

key_point.text: Accommodation is muscular — the ciliary muscle reshapes the lens.

body.text: Fluids fill and nourish; nerves report. Only muscle does mechanical work on the lens.

trap.text: Vitreous humor fills most of the eye but focuses nothing.

text.text: An annular eclipse is formed when
The sun, moon, and earth comes in straight line
One of the sun, moon, and earth are not visible
Two or more stars gathered together
The Earth comes between the moon and the sun

key_point.text: Annular means ring — syzygy with the moon too far for totality.

body.text: Sun, moon and earth aligned with the moon distant leaves a ring of fire. Earth-between-moon-and-sun is a lunar eclipse.

trap.text: The earth-between option describes a lunar eclipse — the wrong body in the middle for a solar ring.

text.text: If a positively charged rod is brought close to the cap in the diagram above, the divergence

key_point.text: A positive rod near the cap drives more positive charge onto the leaves.

body.text: The figure shows diverged, positively charged leaves. The approaching positive rod repels more positive charge down onto them — divergence increases.

trap.text: Collapse needs charge neutralised or removed; adding like charge spreads the leaves wider.

text.text: If the weight of an object on the Earth's surface is 2.5 x 10\(^3\)N, what is its weight on the moon's surface if the gravitational force of the moon is one-sixth of the Earth's(g = 10m/s\(^{-2}\))

key_point.text: Moon weight is one-sixth of Earth weight.

trap.text: Multiplying by 6 answers the reverse trip — the Moon pulls less, not more.

text.text: A boat or airplane has a pointed front or head. This is to

body.text: A pointed head parts the fluid smoothly instead of pushing it — less friction, less drag. Stopping, looks, and more friction are not its job.

trap.text: Increased friction is the opposite of every streamlined shape ever built.

text.text: A gas is cooled at a constant pressure from 57°C was observed to shrink one-fifth (1\5) of its original volume of 2.00cm\(^3\). Find its new temperature

key_point.text: Charles's law in kelvin — and the gas shrinks TO one-fifth.

body.text: V₂ = 2.00/5 = 0.40 cm³. T₂ = 330 × 0.4/2.0 = 66 K = −207°C. (The key forces the TO-one-fifth reading: losing one-fifth would give −9°C, absent from the options.)

trap.text: Reading shrink-one-fifth as lose-one-fifth gives −9°C — present in no option; the key pins the TO reading.

text.text: The gravitational force between two masses, P and Q, is 10N, find the new value of the force if both masses are doubled

key_point.text: Doubling both masses quadruples the pull.

trap.text: 20 N doubles once — both masses double, so the factor squares.

text.text: If the length of a simple pendulum is 120cm, calculate its frequency [\(\pi\) = \(\frac{22}{7}\) g = 10ms\(^{-2}\)]

key_point.text: Pendulum frequency from length — computed 0.46 Hz against option 0.5.

body.text: f = (1/2π)√(g/L) = (7/44)×√(10/1.2) ≈ 0.46 Hz, nearest option 0.5 Hz. The alternatives miss by multiples.

trap.text: 2.8 Hz and 1.2 Hz would need a centimetre-scale pendulum, not 120 cm.

text.text: From the above graph, what is the distance covered in the last stage of the motion?

key_point.text: Last stage is the triangle: half base times height.

body.text: From the figure: 12 m/s flat to 10 s, then linear to zero at 14 s. Last stage 10→14 s: ½×4×12 = 24 m.

trap.text: 56 m reads the whole graph — the question asks the last stage only.

text.text: Assuming E\(_1\), E\(_2\), and E\(_3\), are equal, then the total e.m.f of the arrangement will be given by

key_point.text: Equal emfs in parallel stay one emf.

body.text: The figure puts E₁, E₂, E₃ across the same two nodes: parallel, so E = E₁ = E₂ = E₃.

trap.text: Adding them wires in series — parallel branches share voltage.

text.text: Given that SQ = 10cm and SR = 6cm, the refractive index of the block of glass shown in the above figure is

key_point.text: Index is SQ over SR — the critical-angle reciprocal.

body.text: From the figure the ray geometry gives SQ/SR = 10/6 ≈ 1.67. 0.60 stops at the sine without reciprocating.

trap.text: 0.60 is the sine itself — index is its reciprocal.

text.text: Water waves and light waves differ generally in their

key_point.text: Only mechanical waves need a medium.

body.text: Water waves ride water; light rides nothing. Diffraction, reflection and vibration direction are shared behaviours.

trap.text: Both diffract and reflect — shared behaviours never distinguish.

text.text: placing the magnetic bar in a solenoid
double-stroking the magnet with soft in n-s direction
heating a magnetic bar red hot and allowed to cool e-w direction
hammering the magnetic bar repeatedly in n-s direction

key_point.text: Heat past the Curie point kills magnetism; cooling east-west keeps it dead.

body.text: Red-hot randomises domains; cooling in the neutral orientation freezes them disordered. Solenoids magnetise; stroking and hammering N-S align.

trap.text: Hammering N-S aligns domains — it magnetises, the reverse of the question.

text.text: The electrical power developed in the resistor above is

key_point.text: Power is voltage squared over resistance — 2 Ω on the figure, read close.

body.text: The resistor reads 2 Ω (zoomed against a 3 Ω misread): P = 16²/2 = 128 W.

trap.text: 3 Ω misreads the label and lands at 85 W, present in no option — the figure, zoomed, says 2 Ω.

text.text: When a spiral spring is compressed by an external force of 200 N, it stores 0.16 J of energy. What amount of energy will it store when compressed by an external force of 700 N?

key_point.text: Spring energy scales with force squared.

trap.text: 1.12 J scales linearly (×7) — energy goes as the square.

text.text: A block with an initial speed of 10 m/s slides on a horizontal surface and comes to rest after traveling a distance of 25 m. What is the coefficient of kinetic friction between the block and the surface? (Take g = 9.8 m/s\(^2\)).

key_point.text: Friction work eats the kinetic energy: μ = v²/2gs.

trap.text: 0.5 stops the arithmetic halfway — the full stopping distance sets the scale.

text.text: Which light source operates primarily based on stimulated emission of radiation?

body.text: Laser is light amplification by stimulated emission of radiation. Fluorescent, LED and incandescent emit spontaneously or thermally.

trap.text: LED tempts as modern light tech, but its emission is spontaneous, not stimulated.

text.text: A note written on the second line of the treble staff is:

key_point.text: The treble staff lines, bottom to top, are E G B D F.

body.text: The second line from the bottom carries **G** — the G above middle C. Lines are E, G, B, D, F; spaces are F, A, C, E.

trap.text: Counting from the top gives the fourth line, D — a reliable way to be sure of the wrong answer.

text.text: How many sharps are there in the key signature of E major?

key_point.text: E major has four sharps: F#, C#, G#, D#.

body.text: Every major key adds one sharp to the previous: G has one, D two, A three, **E four**. The last sharp added is always the leading note, D#.

trap.text: E major is often confused with its relative minor, C# minor, which shares the same four sharps — the count is the same either way.

text.text: The ascending interval from C to G is a:

key_point.text: C up to G spans five letter names and 7 semitones: a perfect fifth.

body.text: Count C-D-E-F-G = five, and the distance is 7 semitones, which makes it a **perfect fifth**. Intervals spanning two octaves start again from one.

trap.text: C to F is the fourth — a semitone short of C up to G's seven.

text.text: In a 3/4 time signature, one complete bar contains:

key_point.text: The lower number names the beat: 3/4 means three crotchet (quarter-note) beats to the bar.

body.text: The top number counts beats and the bottom names the note value, so 3/4 is **three crotchets** — the waltz. The top number is not the same as the bottom.

trap.text: Reading the *top* number as a count of four is the standard slip; that would be 4/4.

text.text: The descending form of the major scale from do is:
do re mi fa sol la ti do
do ti la sol fa mi re do
sol la ti do re mi fa sol
mi re do ti la sol fa mi

key_point.text: Going down, the syllables run backwards: do ti la sol fa mi re do.

body.text: The major scale rises do-re-mi-fa-sol-la-ti-do; reversing it gives **do-ti-la-sol-fa-mi-re-do**, which is what you sing descending.

trap.text: Option (a) is the ascending form and looks right until you try to sing it downwards.

text.text: Which of the following is a percussion instrument?

key_point.text: A xylophone sounds when its bars are struck, so it is a percussion instrument.

body.text: Percussion instruments make sound by being **struck**. The xylophone's tuned bars are struck with mallets; the violin, flute and trumpet are all blown or bowed.

trap.text: The piano is also struck in the wider sense, but in school classification it is a keyboard — the xylophone is unambiguous.

body.text: Author of Kitab al-Aghani: Abu al-Faraj al-Isbahani. Ibn Khaldun, Sibawayh and al-Asma'i differ.

trap.text: Ibn-Khaldun tempts as famous-name, but Aghani is Isbahani's.

text.text: أي الجمل التالية تحتوي على فعل مضارع؟

body.text: Only yaktubu al-walad is mudari'. Dhahaba, qara'a and akaltu all past.

trap.text: Qara'a tempts as verb-word, but present is yaktubu.

text.text: رحيمٌ"، ما نوع "إنَّ"؟في الجملة: "إنّ اللهَ غفورٌ

body.text: Inna is harf tawkeed wa nasb. Nafi, 'atf and shart miss its work.

trap.text: 'Atf tempts as particle-talk, but inna stresses.

text.text: في الإسلام، ما هو ركن الصيام؟

body.text: Rukn asked: fasting itself (pillar-of-Islam reading). Hajj, dhikr and zakat are other pillars.

trap.text: Zakat tempts as pillar-word, but the key here is fasting.

body.text: Meaning stated: pen. Book, paper and ink differ.

trap.text: Book tempts as study-word, but qalam is pen.

body.text: Masdar of the mufa'ala form stated. Qatl, maqtal and broken spellings miss it.

trap.text: Qatl tempts as root-word, but the masdar is qitaal.

text.text: من هو أول خليفة في الإسلام؟

body.text: Awwal khalifa stated. Ali, Uthman and Umar follow.

trap.text: Umar tempts as caliph-great, but first was Abu Bakr.

body.text: Trait stated: awzan plus qawafi. Pure prose, tales-only and no-rhetoric invert it.

trap.text: Tales-only tempts as old-poetry, but Jahili weighs.

text.text: ما نوع "لن" في الجملة: "لن أسافرَ غدًّا"؟

body.text: Lan effects nasb (negated future). Istifham, nafi-meaning and jazm miss its government.

trap.text: Jazm tempts as particle-effect, but lan نصبs.

body.text: Born in Egypt stated. Morocco, Syria and Iraq miss Cairo.

trap.text: Syria tempts as poet-land, but Shawqi is Egypt's.

text.text: Answer question below using the passage below. الوقت كالسيف إن لم تقطعه قطعك"، هذا المثل يعكس أهمية استغلال الوقت وعدم تضييع اللحظات التمينة في الكسل أو الإهمال. كما أن "العلم نور والجهل ظلام" يوضح أن العلم ينير العقول ويوجه الإنسان إلى الصواب، في حين أن الجهل يقوده إلى الضياع. كذلك، "الصديق وقت الضيق" مثل يؤكد أن الصديق الحقيقي هو من يبقى إلى جانبك في الأوقات الصعبة، لا من يختفي عند الشدائد. ومن الأقوال المأتورة في الإسلام: "النظافة من الإيمان"، فهي تدل على أن النظافة ليست مجرد عادة، بل جزء أساسي من الإيمان والتقوى. وأخيرًا، يقول أحد الشعراء: "إذا غامرت في شرف مروم فلا تقنع بما .دون النجوم"، دعوة للتمسك بالطموح العالي وعدم الرضا بالقليل إذا أردنا المجد والكرامة ماذا يُفهم من الجملة: "الوقت كالسيف إن لم تقطعه قطعك"؟

body.text: From the passage: precious time must be seized. Slow, worthless and tamable invert the sword.

trap.text: Tamable tempts as control-hope, but time cuts.

text.text: Answer question below using the passage below. الوقت كالسيف إن لم تقطعه قطعك"، هذا المثل يعكس أهمية استغلال الوقت وعدم تضييع اللحظات التمينة في الكسل أو الإهمال كما أن "العلم نور والجهل ظلام" يوضح أن العلم ينير العقول ويوجه الإنسان إلى الصواب، في حين أن الجهل يقوده إلى الضياع. كذلك، "الصديق وقت الضيق" مثل يؤكد أن الصديق الحقيقي هو من يبقى إلى جانبك في الأوقات الصعبة، لا من يختفي عند الشدائد. ومن الأقوال المأتورة في الإسلام: "النظافة من الإيمان"، فهي تدل على أن النظافة ليست مجرد عادة، بل جزء أساسي من الإيمان والتقوى. وأخيرًا، يقول أحد الشعراء: "إذا غامرت في شرف مروم فلا تقنع بما .دون النجوم"، دعوة للتمسك بالطموح العالي وعدم الرضا بالقليل إذا أردنا المجد والكرامة في عبارة: "العلم نور والجهل ظلام"، ما المقصود بالعلم؟
